sentences.zh: 劉保勳

translations.literal: Liu Baoxun
translations.idiomatic: Liu Baoxun

sentences.zh: 劉保勳，字修業，河南人。

translations.literal: Liu Baoxun, style name Xiuye, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Baoxun, whose style name was Xiuye, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 父處讓，仕後唐，入晉拜樞密使，出為彰德軍節度。

translations.literal: His father Liu Churang served the Later Tang; entering Jin he was appointed Military Affairs Commissioner, then sent out as military governor of the Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Churang had served the Later Tang and, after the Jin takeover, was appointed Military Affairs Commissioner before being posted as military governor of the Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 保勳少好騎射。

translations.literal: Baoxun in youth loved riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Baoxun was fond of horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰中，裁十許歲，攝潞州左司馬，隨父署彰德軍衙內都校。

translations.literal: In the Qingtai era of Later Tang, barely ten-some years old, he acted as Left Vice-Marshal of Lu Prefecture and followed his father to an appointment as chief commander within the Zhangde Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai reign of the Later Tang, when he was only about ten, he served as acting Left Vice-Marshal of Lu Prefecture and accompanied his father to a posting as chief commander of the Zhangde Army headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 父卒，補供奉官。

translations.literal: When his father died, he was appointed Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he received an appointment as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 習刑名之學，頗工詩。

translations.literal: He studied penal law and was quite skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He studied penal law and became quite accomplished as a poet.

sentences.zh: 因獻詩，宰相桑維翰奇之，奏擢為太常丞。

translations.literal: Because he presented poems, Chancellor Sang Weihan found him remarkable and memorialized to promote him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted his poems, Chancellor Sang Weihan took notice and recommended him for promotion to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歷漢為秘書丞。

translations.literal: Under Han he served as Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Han he served as Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，有薦其詳練法律，兼大理正，遷工部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun of Zhou, someone recommended his mastery of law; he concurrently served as Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review and was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun reign of Zhou he was recommended for his thorough knowledge of the law, appointed concurrent Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and then promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 歷掌鄆、宋、楚三州鹽、麴、商稅。

translations.literal: He successively supervised salt, monopolized brew, and commercial taxes in Yan, Song, and Chu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to administer the salt, liquor monopoly, and commercial tax operations of Yan, Song, and Chu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋初，拜戶部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was appointed to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty was founded he was appointed to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，起復，出掌蘄口榷茶。

translations.literal: He suffered his mother's death, was recalled from mourning, and sent out to manage the Qiankou tea monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to take charge of the Qiankou tea monopoly.

sentences.zh: 徙雲安監鹽制置使，歲滿，出羨餘百萬，轉運使欲以狀聞，保勳曰：「貪官物為己功，可乎？」

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Salt Commissioner of Yun'an; when his term ended he produced a surplus of a million; the transport commissioner wished to report this in a memorial; Baoxun said: "To take official goods as one's own merit—is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Salt Commissioner of Yun'an, and when his term ended he turned in a surplus of a million cash. The transport commissioner wanted to report this achievement, but Baoxun said, "Can one claim credit by hoarding public property as one's own?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The report was dropped.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，遷司封員外郎、監左藏庫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors and Supervisor of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaibao reign he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors and supervisor of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 六年，知宋州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was made prefect of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he became prefect of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，遷祠部郎中、通判晉州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites and concurrent administrative prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites and assigned as concurrent administrative prefect of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年，選為江南西路轉運使，賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was selected as transport commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit and granted a million cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was chosen as transport commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit and given a gift of a million cash.

sentences.zh: 三年，徙兩浙東北路。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to the Zhejiang East and North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to the Zhejiang East and North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太宗征晉陽，改戶部郎中，為隨軍轉運使兼勾當北面轉運事。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Jinyang, he was changed to Director of the Ministry of Revenue and made army-following transport commissioner concurrently managing northern transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Jinyang, Baoxun was made Director in the Ministry of Revenue and appointed army transport commissioner with concurrent charge of northern transport affairs.

sentences.zh: 又與侯陟同勾當軍前諸事。

translations.literal: He also together with Hou Zhi managed various matters before the army.
translations.idiomatic: He also shared with Hou Zhi the management of various affairs at the front.

sentences.zh: 會陝西北路轉運使雷德驤調發沁州軍糧後期，詔劾德驤，以保勳代之。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi North Circuit transport commissioner Lei Dexiang was late in dispatching Qinzhou army grain, an edict impeached Dexiang and replaced him with Baoxun.
translations.idiomatic: When Lei Dexiang, transport commissioner of the Shaanxi North Circuit, fell behind in dispatching army grain from Qin Prefecture, an imperial edict censured him and replaced him with Baoxun.

sentences.zh: 太原平，命知幷州。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan was pacified, he was ordered to govern Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiyuan was pacified he was appointed prefect of Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 逾年召入，判大理寺，出知昇州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned in, served as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, then sent out to govern Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled to the capital to preside over the Court of Judicial Review, then was posted as prefect of Sheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是冬，召歸，點檢三司開拆司，會鹽鐵使闕，又命權領其事。

translations.literal: That winter he was recalled, inspected the Three Departments' Opening and Unpacking Office; when the Salt and Iron Commissioner post was vacant, he was also ordered to act in that capacity.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was recalled to inspect the Three Departments' Opening and Unpacking Office, and when the post of Salt and Iron Commissioner fell vacant he was also ordered to act in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部郎中兼判三司勾院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of War concurrently judging the Three Departments Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of War with concurrent duty in the Three Departments Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜右諫議大夫，俄知開封府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was appointed Right Remonstrating Grandee; soon he governed Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made Right Remonstrating Grandee and soon afterward became prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 寡婦劉詣府訴夫主前妻子元吉置堇食中，毒己將死。

translations.literal: A widow Liu came to the prefecture to sue, saying her husband's son by a former wife, Yuanji, put hellebore in food and poisoned her nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: A widow surnamed Liu came to the prefectural court alleging that Yuanji, her husband's son by a former wife, had put hellebore in her food and nearly poisoned her to death.

sentences.zh: 按驗獄成，元吉妻撾登聞鼓訴冤，事下御史臺。

translations.literal: Upon investigation the case was concluded; Yuanji's wife beat the Petition Drum to plead injustice, and the matter was sent down to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After investigation the case was closed, but Yuanji's wife beat the Petition Drum to protest injustice, and the matter was referred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 其實劉有姦狀，元吉知之，劉慙悸成疾，故誣告之。

translations.literal: In fact Liu had committed adultery; Yuanji knew it; Liu, ashamed and fearful, fell ill, and therefore falsely accused him.
translations.idiomatic: In fact the widow Liu had been unfaithful; Yuanji knew of it, and Liu, consumed by shame and fear, fell ill and therefore brought a false accusation.

sentences.zh: 保勳坐奪奉三月，俄以辛仲甫代之。

translations.literal: Baoxun was punished by forfeiture of salary for three months; soon Xin Zhongfu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun was penalized with three months' forfeiture of salary, and soon Xin Zhongfu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復判大理寺。

translations.literal: Before long, he again presided over the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed to preside over the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，權御史中丞兼勾當差遣院。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he acted as Vice Censor-in-Chief concurrently managing the Assignment Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he served as acting Vice Censor-in-Chief with concurrent charge of the Assignment Office.

sentences.zh: 是秋，罷權中丞。

translations.literal: That autumn, he was removed from acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was relieved of his acting post as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 三年春，命曹彬等征幽州，保勳以本官知幽州行府事。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year, Cao Bin and others were ordered to campaign against Youzhou; Baoxun in his existing office managed affairs of the Youzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year Cao Bin and others were ordered to campaign against Youzhou, and Baoxun retained his rank while taking charge of affairs at the Youzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 子利涉以開封府兵曹督芻粟隨軍，常從其父。

translations.literal: His son Lishe, as Kaifeng Prefecture military aide, supervised fodder and grain with the army and often followed his father.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lishe served as military aide of Kaifeng Prefecture supervising fodder and grain with the army and usually accompanied his father.

sentences.zh: 會王師不利，濟拒馬河，更相蹂躪，多死。

translations.literal: When the imperial army met misfortune, crossing the Juma River they trampled one another, and many died.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army met defeat, men crossing the Juma River trampled one another in the confusion, and many perished.

sentences.zh: 保勳馬陷淖中，利涉自後掀出之，力不勝，人馬相擠壓，遂俱死。

translations.literal: Baoxun's horse sank in the mire; Lishe from behind lifted him out; his strength failed; men and horses pressed together, and both died.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun's horse sank in the mire; Lishe tried to lift him out from behind, but his strength gave way as men and horses pressed in upon them, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 時年六十二。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-two years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 上命恤其後。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered relief for his survivors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that his survivors be cared for.

sentences.zh: 保勳三子，二子先保勳死，季子隨沒。

translations.literal: Baoxun had three sons; two died before Baoxun; the youngest perished with him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun had three sons; two had died before him, and the youngest perished with him.

sentences.zh: 以其孫巨川為嗣，授秘書正字。

translations.literal: His grandson Juchuan was made heir and granted Secretary Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Juchuan was established as his heir and appointed Secretary Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，特召贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he was specially summoned and posthumously granted Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong reign he was specially honored with a posthumous appointment as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 保勳性純謹，少寐，未嘗忤物，精於吏事，不憚繁劇。

translations.literal: Baoxun's nature was pure and cautious; he slept little; he never gave offense; he was expert in clerical affairs and did not shrink from complexity.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun was by nature pure and cautious, slept little, never gave offense to others, was expert in administrative matters, and did not shrink from arduous duties.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「吾受君命未嘗辭避，接同僚未嘗失意，居家積貲未嘗至千錢。」

translations.literal: He once told others: "I have never declined or evaded an imperial commission; in dealing with colleagues I have never lost their regard; at home my accumulated wealth has never reached a thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: He once told others, "I have never declined an imperial commission; in dealing with colleagues I have never lost their goodwill; and the wealth I have accumulated at home has never reached a thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 及死，聞者皆痛惜之。

translations.literal: When he died, all who heard grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, all who heard of it grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，又錄其次孫世長為正字。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao, his second grandson Shichang was also enrolled as Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhidao his second grandson Shichang was also appointed Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，保勳妻卒，詔賜錢十萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, Baoxun's wife died; an edict granted a hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping reign Baoxun's wife died, and an edict granted a hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 巨川，累為比部郎中。

translations.literal: Juchuan successively served as Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Juchuan rose through several posts to Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau.

sentences.zh: 滕中正

translations.literal: Teng Zhongzheng
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zhongzheng

sentences.zh: 滕中正，字普光，青州北海人。

translations.literal: Teng Zhongzheng, style name Puguang, was a man of Beihai in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zhongzheng, whose style name was Puguang, came from Beihai in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖瑤，高郵令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yao was magistrate of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yao had been magistrate of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 祖煦，即墨令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xu was magistrate of Jimo.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xu had been magistrate of Jimo.

sentences.zh: 父保裔，興平令。

translations.literal: His father Baoyi was magistrate of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Baoyi had been magistrate of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 中正弱冠，舉進士不第。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng at coming of age took the jinshi examination but did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: At coming of age Zhongzheng took the jinshi examination but failed to pass.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，滑帥向拱奏辟為掌書記。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, the military governor of Hua, Xiang Gong, memorialized to appoint him Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande reign of Zhou the military governor of Hua, Xiang Gong, recommended him for appointment as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 拱移鎮彭門，會中正丁外艱，復表奪情，仍署舊職，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: When Gong was transferred to govern Pengmen, Zhongzheng was in mourning for his father; Gong again memorialized to seize his feelings and retain him in his old post, adding Gentleman for Dispersing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong was transferred to Peng Gate, Zhongzheng was mourning his father; Gong memorialized to have him recalled from mourning and kept in his former post, with the added rank of Gentleman for Dispersing Affairs.

sentences.zh: 拱鎮襄陽，以中正為襄、均、房、復觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Gong governed Xiangyang, he made Zhongzheng administrative aide of the Xiang, Jun, Fang, and Fu observation circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Gong governed Xiangyang he appointed Zhongzheng administrative aide of the Xiang, Jun, Fang, and Fu observation circuit.

sentences.zh: 及留守西洛，又奏署河南府判官、檢校戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: When he remained to guard Western Luoyang, he again memorialized to appoint him administrative aide of Henan Prefecture and Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Western Luoyang he again recommended Zhongzheng as administrative aide of Henan Prefecture and Acting Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，度支員外郎侯陟表中正有材幹，入為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande, Revenue Vice Director Hou Zhi memorialized that Zhongzheng had talent and ability; he entered service as Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande, Revenue Vice Director Hou Zhi recommended Zhongzheng for his ability, and he was appointed Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 兩川平，選知興元府，判西京留臺，俄通判河南府留守司事。

translations.literal: When the Two Chuan were pacified, he was selected to govern Xingyuan Prefecture and judge the Western Capital Remaining Court; soon he was concurrent administrative prefect of the Henan Prefecture Remaining Court.
translations.idiomatic: After the Two Chuan were pacified he was chosen prefect of Xingyuan and judge of the Western Capital Remaining Court, and soon served as concurrent administrative prefect of the Henan Remaining Court.

sentences.zh: 太祖雩祀西洛，以祗事之勤，轉倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Taizu performed the rain prayer sacrifice at Western Luoyang, for his diligent service he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu performed the rain-prayer sacrifice at Western Luoyang, Zhongzheng was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Granaries for his diligent service.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年春，大宴，上歡甚，以虛盞示群臣。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Yongxi, at a great banquet the emperor was very merry and showed the ministers an empty cup.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Yongxi, at a grand banquet the emperor was in high spirits and held up an empty cup to his ministers.

sentences.zh: 宰相言飲酒過度，恐有失儀之責。

translations.literal: The chancellor said that drinking to excess might incur blame for breach of decorum.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor said that excessive drinking might lead to charges of impropriety.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂中正曰：「今君臣相遇，有失者勿彈劾也。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Zhongzheng and said: "Today ruler and ministers meet; if anyone errs, do not impeach him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Zhongzheng and said, "Today ruler and ministers are together; if anyone errs, do not impeach him."

sentences.zh: 因是伶官盛言宴會之樂，上曰：「朕樂在時平民安。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the entertainers greatly praised the joys of feasting; the emperor said: "My joy lies in the peace of the people in their season."
translations.idiomatic: The entertainers then lavishly praised the pleasures of the feast, and the emperor said, "My joy lies in the peace of the people in their season."

sentences.zh: 是冬乾明節，群臣上壽酒，既三行，上目中正曰：「三爵之飲，實惟常禮，朕欲與群臣更舉一卮，可乎？」

translations.literal: That winter on the Qianming festival, when the ministers presented birthday wine, after three rounds the emperor looked at Zhongzheng and said: "Three rounds of drinking are indeed the regular rite; I wish to raise one more cup with the ministers—is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: That winter on the Qianming festival, after the ministers had presented birthday wine and three rounds had been drunk, the emperor looked at Zhongzheng and said, "Three rounds are the regular rite; I wish to raise one more cup with you all—may I?"

sentences.zh: 中正曰：「陛下聖恩甚厚，臣敢不奉詔。」

translations.literal: Zhongzheng said: "Your Majesty's sage grace is very generous; how dare your servant not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng replied, "Your Majesty's gracious favor is very great; how dare your servant not obey the edict?"

sentences.zh: 殿上皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: All in the hall shouted "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the hall shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 二年，以年老辭，出知河南府。

translations.literal: In the second year, citing old age he resigned and was sent out to govern Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he resigned on grounds of age and was appointed prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，被病罷，分司西京。

translations.literal: Before long, stricken by illness he was dismissed and assigned to the Western Capital Remaining Court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill and was relieved of duty, assigned to the Western Capital Remaining Court.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，判留司御史臺，命其子玄錫權河南司錄以便養。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, he judged the Remaining Censorate and was ordered to have his son Xuanxi act as Henan Registrar for his convenience in supporting him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua reign he presided over the Remaining Censorate and had his son Xuanxi appointed acting Henan Registrar so he could be cared for at home.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 中正性峻刻，連鞫大獄，時議以為深文。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng's nature was harsh and severe; he continuously tried major cases, and opinion at the time held that his judgments were overly strict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng was harsh by nature; he repeatedly tried major cases, and contemporaries regarded his judgments as overly severe.

sentences.zh: 權中丞日，振舉綱憲，人以稱職許之。

translations.literal: On the days when he acted as Vice Censor-in-Chief, he raised the standards of law and regulation, and people acknowledged him as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: While acting as Vice Censor-in-Chief he enforced the laws vigorously, and people acknowledged that he fulfilled his duties.

sentences.zh: 二子並舉進士，玄錫至刑部郎中，玄晏後名世寧，至工部郎中。

translations.literal: Both sons passed the jinshi examination; Xuanxi rose to Director of the Ministry of Punishments, and Xuanyan later took the name Shining and rose to Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Both sons passed the jinshi examination; Xuanxi rose to Director in the Ministry of Punishments, and Xuanyan later took the name Shining and rose to Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 劉蟠，字士龍，濱州渤海人。

translations.literal: Liu Pan, style name Shilong, was a man of Bohai in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pan, whose style name was Shilong, came from Bohai in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年舉進士，解褐益都主簿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyou of Han he passed the jinshi examination and began service as chief clerk of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyou of Han he passed the jinshi examination and took his first post as chief clerk of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 宋初，歷安遠軍及河陽節度推官、保義軍掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he successively served as investigating censor of Anyuan Army and of Heyang Circuit and as Recorder of Baoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served successively as investigating censor of Anyuan Army and Heyang Circuit and as Recorder of Baoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，召拜監察御史，典染院事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande, he was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor and placed in charge of the Dyeing Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande he was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor with charge of the Dyeing Bureau.

sentences.zh: 初，蘇曉掌京城市征，頗幹集，及卒，選蟠代之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Su Xiao had managed the capital city's levies and was quite capable at collection; when he died, Pan was chosen to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Su Xiao had managed the capital levies with notable efficiency; when he died, Pan was chosen to replace him.

sentences.zh: 冬，命為太宗生辰使。

translations.literal: In winter he was appointed birthday envoy to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed birthday envoy to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 開寶七年，與殿中丞劉德言同知淮南諸州轉運事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaibao, together with Palace Director Liu Deyan he concurrently managed transport affairs for the Huainan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaibao he and Palace Director Liu Deyan jointly managed transport affairs for the Huainan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，就遷倉部員外郎，改轉運使，歲漕江東米四百萬斛以給京師，頗為稱職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was promoted in place to Vice Director of the Ministry of Granaries, then made transport commissioner; each year he transported four million hu of Jiangdong rice to supply the capital and was quite regarded as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he was promoted in place to Vice Director in the Ministry of Granaries and then made transport commissioner; each year he shipped four million hu of Jiangdong rice to the capital and was widely regarded as competent.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，部內僧道乞留，詔許再任，賜金紫，改駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: When his term ended, monks and Daoists within his jurisdiction begged that he remain; an edict permitted reappointment, granted gold and purple, and changed him to Vice Director of the Ministry of Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, monks and Daoists in his circuit petitioned to keep him; an edict allowed reappointment, granted him gold and purple insignia, and promoted him to Vice Director in the Ministry of Carriages.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁內艱，時以諸州綱運留滯，起復，知京城陸路發運司事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, in mourning for his mother, because transport convoys from the prefectures were delayed, he was recalled from mourning and made to manage the capital's overland transport dispatch office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, while mourning his mother, he was recalled from mourning because transport convoys were backing up and was put in charge of the capital's overland transport dispatch office.

sentences.zh: 會河決韓村，大發丁夫塞之，命蟠調給其餉，未幾河塞。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke at Hancun, corvée labor was greatly mobilized to block it; Pan was ordered to supply their provisions; before long the river was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke at Hancun and corvée labor was mobilized to block it, Pan was ordered to supply their provisions; before long the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方議封禪，以蟠為東封水陸計度轉運使，會詔罷其禮。

translations.literal: The court was then discussing the Feng and Shan sacrifices and appointed Pan eastern Feng land-and-water planning transport commissioner; soon an edict abolished the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then planning the Feng and Shan sacrifices and appointed Pan eastern Feng land-and-water planning transport commissioner, but soon an edict canceled the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 俄遷工部郎中，充河北水路轉運使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Works and made Hebei water-route transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Works and appointed Hebei water-route transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 改刑部郎中，就充水陸轉運使，入判本部事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Ministry of Punishments, then filled the post of land-and-water transport commissioner and entered to judge affairs of his ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director in the Ministry of Punishments, then served as land-and-water transport commissioner and entered the capital to judge affairs of his ministry.

sentences.zh: 籍田畢，遷左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the plowing ceremony was completed, he was transferred to Left Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: After the plowing ceremony he was promoted to Left Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，兼同考京朝官差遣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua, he concurrently participated in evaluating capital officials' assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua reign he also took part in evaluating assignments for capital officials.

sentences.zh: 二年，暴中風眩，上遣太醫視之，賜以金丹。

translations.literal: In the second year he suddenly suffered wind dizziness; the emperor sent the imperial physician to examine him and granted golden elixir pills.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he suddenly suffered a stroke; the emperor sent the imperial physician to treat him and granted golden elixir pills.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 賜錢十萬，給其喪事。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand cash was granted to provide for his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted a hundred thousand cash for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 蟠性清介寡合，能攻苦食淡，專事苛刻，好設奇詐，以售知人主。

translations.literal: Pan's nature was pure and aloof, little given to company; he could endure hardship and eat plain food, devoted himself to harshness, loved to devise strange schemes to win the ruler's recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Pan was pure and aloof by nature, kept few companions, could endure hardship and plain fare, specialized in harsh methods, and liked to devise clever schemes to win the ruler's favor.

sentences.zh: 典染作日，太祖多臨視之，蟠偵車駕至，輒衣短後衣，芒屩持梃以督役，頭蓬不治，遽出迎謁。

translations.literal: On days when he managed the dye works, Taizu often came to inspect; Pan would spy when the imperial carriage arrived, then put on short rear-guard clothes, straw sandals, and a staff to supervise the workers, his hair unkempt and uncombed, and rush out to bow in audience.
translations.idiomatic: While managing the dye works Pan noticed when Taizu came to inspect; as soon as the imperial carriage arrived he would put on a workman's short jacket and straw sandals, take a staff to supervise labor with unkempt hair, and rush out to receive the emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖以為勤事，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: Taizu thought him diligent in duty and granted two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took this as proof of diligent service and granted him two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 嘗受詔巡茶淮南，部民私販者眾。

translations.literal: He once received an edict to inspect tea in Huainan; within his jurisdiction private traders were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He once received an edict to inspect tea in Huainan, where private traders were numerous in his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 蟠乘羸馬，偽稱商人，抵民家求市茶，民家不疑，出與之，即擒置於法。

translations.literal: Pan rode a weak horse, falsely claiming to be a merchant, came to a household to buy tea; the household did not suspect him, brought tea out to him, and he immediately seized them and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Pan rode a weak horse and posed as a merchant, went to a household to buy tea; when the family unsuspectingly brought tea out, he seized them and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 子鍇，初以父蔭為大理評事，咸平二年，擢進士第。

translations.literal: His son Kai, at first through his father's privilege was made Court of Judicial Review reviewer; in the second year of Xianping he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai first entered service through his father's privilege as a Court of Judicial Review reviewer; in the second year of Xianping he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻《幸太學頌》。

translations.literal: He once presented "Ode on the Imperial Visit to the Imperial College."
translations.idiomatic: He once presented an "Ode on the Imperial Visit to the Imperial College."

sentences.zh: 真宗中夜觀書，得鍇頌，頗嘉賞之，出以示輔臣，且言鍇幼孤，能自立，召試，命直史館。

translations.literal: Zhenzong in the middle of the night was reading and obtained Kai's ode; he greatly admired it, showed it to his chief ministers, and added Kai had been orphaned young yet could stand on his own; he was summoned for examination and ordered to serve in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Reading late at night, Zhenzong came upon Kai's ode, admired it greatly, showed it to his chief ministers, and said that though Kai had been orphaned young he had made his own way; Kai was summoned for examination and appointed to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 累遷至戶部郎中、鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron.

sentences.zh: 孔承恭

translations.literal: Kong Chenggong
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chenggong

sentences.zh: 孔承恭，字光祖，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Kong Chenggong, style name Guangzu, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chenggong, whose style name was Guangzu, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗東遷，舉族隨之，遂占籍河南。

translations.literal: When Tang Zhaozong moved east, the whole clan followed and thus registered their household in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong of Tang moved east, the whole clan followed him and registered their household in Henan.

sentences.zh: 五世祖戡，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan has a biography in the Book of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan has a biography in the Book of Tang.

sentences.zh: 戡孫迥，萊州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhan's grandson Jiong was prefect of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's grandson Jiong was prefect of Lai.

sentences.zh: 迥子昌庶，虞部郎中。

translations.literal: Jiong's son Changshu was Director of the Ministry of Parks.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's son Changshu was Director in the Ministry of Parks.

sentences.zh: 昌庶子莊，仕晉為右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Changshu's son Zhuang served Jin as Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Changshu's son Zhuang served the Jin as Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 由戡至莊，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: From Zhan to Zhuang, all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhan to Zhuang, all had passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 承恭，莊之子也。

translations.literal: Chenggong was Zhuang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong was Zhuang's son.

sentences.zh: 以門蔭授秘書省正字，歷溫、安豐二縣主簿。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed Secretary Proofreader and successively served as chief clerk of Wen and Anfeng counties.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he was appointed Secretary Proofreader and served successively as chief clerk of Wen and Anfeng counties.

sentences.zh: 時王審琦節制壽春，以承恭名家子，奏攝節度推官。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shenqi governed Shouchun and, because Chenggong was the son of a famous family, memorialized to appoint him acting investigating censor of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shenqi governed Shouchun he memorialized to appoint Chenggong, as the son of a distinguished family, acting investigating censor of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 府罷，調補鄭州錄事參軍，入為大理寺丞。

translations.literal: When the headquarters was abolished, he was transferred to supplement Zhengzhou Recorder and entered as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the headquarters was abolished he was transferred to Recorder of Zheng Prefecture and then entered service as Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 獻宮詞，託意求進。

translations.literal: He presented palace lyrics, intending by allusion to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He presented palace lyrics with allusions intended to seek advancement.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒其引喻非宜，免所居官，放歸田里。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry that his analogies were improper, removed him from office, and sent him back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was angered by his improper allusions, stripped him of office, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以赦復授舊官。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, through the amnesty he was again granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong acceded to the throne, an amnesty restored him to his former office.

sentences.zh: 時初榷酒，以承恭監西京酒麴，歲增課六千萬。

translations.literal: At that time the wine monopoly was first established; Chenggong was made to supervise Western Capital wine and brew, increasing revenue by sixty million each year.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine monopoly was first established Chenggong was put in charge of Western Capital wine and brew and increased annual revenue by sixty million.

sentences.zh: 遷大理正，議獄平允，擢庫部員外郎，判大理少卿事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; his deliberations on cases were fair and balanced; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Stores and judged affairs as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; his case deliberations were fair, and he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Stores with concurrent duty as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 遷屯田、兵部二郎中，同考校京朝官課第。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministries of Agriculture and War and jointly evaluated capital officials' performance grades.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director in the Ministries of Agriculture and War and took part in evaluating the performance grades of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 端拱三年，下詔曰：「九寺三監，國之羽儀，制度聲名，往往而在。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duangong, an edict was issued: "The Nine Temples and Three Commissions are the state's ceremonial regalia; their institutions and reputations are often preserved.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duangong an edict declared, "The Nine Temples and Three Commissions are the ceremonial regalia of the state; their institutions and reputations are often preserved.

sentences.zh: 各有副貳，率其司存，品秩素高，職任尤重。

translations.literal: Each has deputies who lead their offices; their ranks are inherently high and their duties especially weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Each has deputies who lead their offices; their ranks are inherently high and their duties especially weighty.

sentences.zh: 郎吏遷授，斯為舊章。

translations.literal: Promotion of clerical officials to these posts is the old regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion of clerical officials to these posts is the established regulation.

sentences.zh: 比聞縉紳之流，頗以臺閣自許，目為散地，甚無謂焉。

translations.literal: Recently it has been heard that among the gentry many regard the terrace pavilions as their own domain and call other posts scattered assignments—this is very meaningless.
translations.idiomatic: Recently it has been heard that many among the gentry regard terrace posts as their proper domain and call other offices scattered assignments—this is quite meaningless.

sentences.zh: 朕將振之，自我而始。

translations.literal: I shall revive them, beginning with myself.
translations.idiomatic: I shall revive them, beginning with myself.

sentences.zh: 其以兵部郎中孔承恭為太常少卿，魏羽為秘書少監，戶部郎中柴成務為光祿少卿，魏庠為衛尉少卿，張洎為太僕少卿，呂端為大理少卿，臧丙為司農少卿，袁廓為鴻臚少卿，工部郎中張雍為太府少卿。」

translations.literal: Let War Ministry Director Kong Chenggong be made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Wei Yu Vice Director of the Secretariat, Revenue Director Chai Chengwu Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Wei Xiang Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Guards, Zhang Bai Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Lü Duan Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Zang Bing Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, Yuan Kuo Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets, Works Director Zhang Yong Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury."
translations.idiomatic: War Ministry Director Kong Chenggong was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Wei Yu, Vice Director of the Secretariat; Revenue Director Chai Chengwu, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Wei Xiang, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Guards; Zhang Bai, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Lü Duan, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review; Zang Bing, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries; Yuan Kuo, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets; and Works Director Zhang Yong, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury."

sentences.zh: 又以屯田郎中雷有終為少府少監，虞部郎中索湘為將作少監。

translations.literal: Revenue Director Lei Youzhong was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Manufactories, and Parks Director Suo Xiang Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Works."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Director Lei Youzhong was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Manufactories, and Parks Director Suo Xiang Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Works.

sentences.zh: 時裴祚、慎從吉、宋雄先為少卿，皆改授東宮官。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Zuo, Shen Congji, and Song Xiong had earlier been vice directors and were all reassigned as Eastern Palace officials.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Zuo, Shen Congji, and Song Xiong had already served as vice directors and were all reassigned as Eastern Palace officials.

sentences.zh: 又詔承恭與左散騎常侍徐鉉刊正道書，俄以疾求解官，且言早遊嵩、少間，樂其風土，願卜居焉。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Chenggong together with Left Regular Attendant Xu Xuan to collate and correct the Daoist canon; soon, ill, he requested to resign office and added he had long traveled between Song and Shao and loved their climate and wished to settle there.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered Chenggong and Left Regular Attendant Xu Xuan to collate the Daoist canon; soon, ill, he asked to resign and said he had long loved the climate of the Song and Shao mountains and wished to settle there.

sentences.zh: 上召見，哀其羸瘠，出御藥賜之，授將作監致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him, pitied his emaciation, sent out imperial medicine to grant him, and appointed him Director of Imperial Works with permission to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him, pitied his wasted frame, sent out imperial medicine, and appointed him Director of Imperial Works with permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 以其子玢同學究出身，為登封縣尉，俾就祿養。

translations.literal: His son Bin, who had passed the classicist examination, was made Dengfeng county lieutenant so he could draw salary to support his father.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin, who had passed the classicist examination, was made lieutenant of Dengfeng so he could draw salary to support his father.

sentences.zh: 未果行而卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: Before he could go he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he died, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 承恭少疏縱，及長，能折節自勵。

translations.literal: Chenggong was unrestrained in youth; when grown he could restrain himself and exert effort.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong was unrestrained in youth, but as an adult he learned to restrain himself and work hard.

sentences.zh: 嘗上疏請令州縣長吏詢訪耆老，求知民間疾苦、吏治得失，及舉令文「賤避貴，少避長，輕避重，去避來」，請詔京兆並諸州於要害處設木牌刻其字，違者論如律。

translations.literal: He once memorialized requesting that prefectural and county chief officials inquire of the elderly to learn the people's hardships, the gains and losses of official administration, and citing the statute text "the base avoid the noble, the few avoid the many, the light avoid the heavy, the departing avoid the arriving," requested an edict that Jingzhao and all prefectures set wooden boards at key places carving these words, with violators punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized that prefectural and county chiefs should inquire of the elderly about popular hardships and administrative failings, and citing the statute "the base avoid the noble, the few avoid the many, the light avoid the heavy, the departing avoid the arriving," asked that Jingzhao and all prefectures set wooden boards at key points carving these words, with violators punished by law.

sentences.zh: 上皆為行之。

translations.literal: The emperor carried out all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor implemented all of his proposals.

sentences.zh: 尤奉佛，多蔬食，所得奉祿，大半以飯僧。

translations.literal: He especially revered Buddhism, ate mostly vegetables, and gave most of his salary to feed monks.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially devoted to Buddhism, ate mostly vegetables, and gave most of his salary to feed monks.

sentences.zh: 嘗勸上不殺人，又請於征戰地修寺及普度僧尼，人多言其迂闊云。

translations.literal: He once urged the emperor not to kill people and also requested temples be built on battlefields and monks and nuns universally released; many said he was impractical.
translations.idiomatic: He once urged the emperor not to take life and also asked that temples be built on battlefields and monks and nuns universally released; many called him impractical.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，轉比部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongxi reign he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau.

sentences.zh: 在任凡六年，召歸，面賜金紫，授度支判官。

translations.literal: In office altogether six years, he was summoned back; in person he was granted gold and purple and appointed Revenue Auditor.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in office he was recalled; the emperor personally granted him gold and purple insignia and appointed him Revenue Auditor.

sentences.zh: 俄遷屯田郎中、知益州，屬歲饑多盜，璫始至，以方略擒捕招輯，盜皆首伏屏息，下詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Agriculture and made prefect of Yizhou; it happened to be a year of famine with many bandits; when Dang first arrived, by strategy he captured and pacified them; all the bandits surrendered and fell silent; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Director in the Ministry of Agriculture and prefect of Yizhou; famine had bred many bandits, but when Dang arrived he captured and pacified them by strategy until all surrendered and fell silent; an edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，就拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he was promoted in place to Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong reign he was promoted in place to Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 時兩川轉運使副皆坐事免，以璫為西川轉運使，加左諫議大夫，改知陝州。

translations.literal: At that time the deputy transport commissioners of the Two Chuan were all dismissed for offenses; Dang was made Western Chuan transport commissioner, added Left Remonstrating Grandee, and changed to govern Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the deputy transport commissioners of the Two Chuan were all dismissed for offenses, Dang was made Western Chuan transport commissioner with the added rank of Left Remonstrating Grandee, then transferred to govern Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，三吳歲饑、疾病，民多死，擇長吏養治之，命璫知蘇州。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era the Three Wu regions suffered famine and disease year after year and many people died; long-term officials were chosen to nurture and treat them, and Dang was ordered to govern Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era the Three Wu regions suffered repeated famine and disease and many died; the court chose experienced officials to care for the people and appointed Dang prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 璫體豐碩，素病足，至州，地卑濕，疾益甚。

translations.literal: Dang had a large frame and had long suffered from foot ailment; reaching the prefecture, the ground was low and damp and his illness grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Dang was stout of build and had long suffered from foot ailments; the prefecture was low and damp and his illness grew worse.

sentences.zh: 人或勸其謝疾北歸，璫曰：「天子以民病俾我綏撫，我以身病而辭焉，非臣子之義也。」

translations.literal: Some urged him to resign on grounds of illness and return north; Dang said: "The Son of Heaven appointed me to soothe the people because they are sick; if I resign because I am sick, that is not the duty of a minister."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to resign and return north on grounds of illness; Dang said, "The Son of Heaven sent me to soothe the people in their sickness; if I resign because of my own illness, that is not the duty of a minister."

sentences.zh: 既而太白犯南斗，曰：「斗為吳分，民方饑，天象如此，長吏得無咎乎！」

translations.literal: Soon Great White invaded the Southern Dipper; he said: "The Dipper is Wu's allotment; the people are starving; with the heavens thus, can a chief official be without blame!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Great White invaded the Southern Dipper; he said, "The Dipper is Wu's allotment and the people are starving; with the heavens thus, can a chief official escape blame?"

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 上聞之嗟悼，錄其子明遠為蒲城主簿，俾護其喪歸葬焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he sighed in grief, enrolled his son Mingyuan as chief clerk of Pucheng, and had him escort the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard he sighed in grief, enrolled his son Mingyuan as chief clerk of Pucheng, and had him escort the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 璫性清簡，歷官三十年，未嘗問家事，唯聚書以貽子孫。

translations.literal: Dang's nature was pure and simple; in office thirty years he never inquired into household affairs and only collected books to leave his sons and grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: Dang was pure and simple by nature; in thirty years of office he never inquired into household affairs and only collected books for his descendants.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「使不忘本也。」

translations.literal: He said: "To make them not forget their roots."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "So they will not forget their roots."

sentences.zh: 明遠，淳化三年進士，後為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Mingyuan passed the jinshi in the third year of Chunhua and later became Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan passed the jinshi in the third year of Chunhua and later became Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 次子柔遠，亦舉進士及第。

translations.literal: The second son Rouyuan also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Rouyuan also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 垂遠，閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Chuiyuan was Attendant of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chuiyuan served as Attendant of the Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 袁廓，劍州梓潼人。

translations.literal: Yuan Kuo, a man of Zitong in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kuo came from Zitong in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在蜀舉進士及第。

translations.literal: In Shu he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 入宋，補雙流縣主簿。

translations.literal: Entering Song, he was appointed chief clerk of Shuangliu County.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Song he was appointed chief clerk of Shuangliu County.

sentences.zh: 又為西平縣主簿，勾稽漏籍，得民丁萬餘，州將薦其勤職，就遷上蔡令，又以課最，擢太子右贊善大夫，令於御史府分領推事，掌榷貨務。

translations.literal: He also served as chief clerk of Xiping County; auditing omitted registers he found more than ten thousand male subjects; the prefect recommended his diligence; he was promoted in place to magistrate of Shangcai; again for outstanding performance he was promoted to Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and ordered to divide investigative duties at the Censorate and manage the monopoly goods office.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as chief clerk of Xiping; auditing omitted registers he found more than ten thousand male subjects; the prefect recommended his diligence and he was promoted in place to magistrate of Shangcai; again for outstanding performance he was made Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent, assigned to divide investigative duties at the Censorate, and put in charge of the monopoly goods office.

sentences.zh: 廓性誇誕，敢大言，好詆訐，太祖以奇士待之。

translations.literal: Kuo's nature was boastful and extravagant; he dared speak boldly and loved to slander; Taizu treated him as an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was boastful by nature, spoke boldly, and loved to slander others; Taizu treated him as an extraordinary man.

sentences.zh: 會秦王廷美遷置房州，以崇儀副使閻彥進知州事，廓通判州事，並賜白金三百兩。

translations.literal: When Prince Qin Tingmei was reassigned to Fang Prefecture, Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies Yan Yanjin was made to govern the prefecture; Kuo was concurrent administrative prefect and both were granted three hundred taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qin Tingmei was reassigned to Fang Prefecture, Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies Yan Yanjin was made prefect and Kuo concurrent administrative prefect; both were granted three hundred taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 廓俄轉殿中侍御史，召為戶部判官，命與陳恕、李惟清專計度芻糧事。

translations.literal: Soon Kuo was transferred to Palace Censor, summoned as Revenue Auditor, and ordered together with Chen Shu and Li Weiqing to specialize in planning fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kuo was transferred to Palace Censor, summoned as Revenue Auditor, and ordered with Chen Shu and Li Weiqing to specialize in planning fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 改戶部員外郎，又為度支判官。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and again made Revenue Auditor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and again Revenue Auditor.

sentences.zh: 籍田，轉本曹郎中，判戶部勾院。

translations.literal: At the plowing ceremony he was transferred to Director of his ministry and judged the Revenue Audit Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the plowing ceremony he was made Director of his ministry and judge of the Revenue Audit Office.

sentences.zh: 廓強項好爭，數與判使等較曲直於上前，聲氣俱厲，上每優容之。

translations.literal: Kuo was obstinate and quarrelsome; he repeatedly argued right and wrong with the auditors before the emperor, both voices fierce; the emperor always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was obstinate and quarrelsome; he repeatedly argued points of right and wrong with the auditors before the emperor in fierce tones, yet the emperor always treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 然勾稽精密，由是部領擁積，為郡吏所訴，詔御史辨問，廓謁見宰相趙普自理。

translations.literal: Yet his auditing was precise; because of this accumulated backlogs in his department were complained of by circuit clerks; an edict ordered the censorate to investigate; Kuo called on Chancellor Zhao Pu to plead his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his auditing was precise; backlogs in his department drew complaints from circuit clerks; an edict ordered the censorate to investigate, and Kuo called on Chancellor Zhao Pu to plead his own case.

sentences.zh: 屬鄭州團練使侯莫陳利用得罪，廓嘗與利用書劄往還稔昵。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhengzhou training commissioner Hou Mo Chen Liyong had committed an offense; Kuo had often exchanged letters with Liyong on familiar terms.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Zhengzhou training commissioner Hou Mo Chen Liyong had committed an offense; Kuo had often exchanged familiar letters with Liyong.

sentences.zh: 普謂之曰：「職司常事，此不足云，與利用交結款密，於理可乎？」

translations.literal: Pu said to him: "Routine duties of office—this is not worth mentioning; but intimate association with Liyong—is that permissible in principle?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu said to him, "Routine office matters are not worth mentioning, but intimate association with Liyong—is that permissible in principle?"

sentences.zh: 廓驚慚泣下，不能對。

translations.literal: Kuo, startled and ashamed, wept and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo, startled and ashamed, wept and could not reply.

sentences.zh: 數日，出知溫州。

translations.literal: Several days later he was sent out to govern Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was sent out as prefect of Wen.

sentences.zh: 就遷鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted in place to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in place to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets.

sentences.zh: 同郡袁仁甫掌州之關征，素以宗盟之分，頗相親善，一旦不協，互有論奏。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Yuan Renpu managed the prefecture's transit duties; by clan ties they were quite friendly; one day they fell out and each memorialized against the other.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Yuan Renpu managed the prefecture's transit duties; as clansmen they had been quite friendly, but one day they fell out and each memorialized against the other.

sentences.zh: 上遣光祿寺丞牛韶往按驗，韶至，並攝繫獄置對。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Revenue Temple Director Niu Shao to investigate; Shao arrived and detained both in prison for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Revenue Temple Director Niu Shao to investigate; when Shao arrived he detained both in prison for questioning.

sentences.zh: 上疑廓被誣，驛召赴闕。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Kuo had been slandered and summoned him post-haste to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Kuo had been slandered and summoned him post-haste to court.

sentences.zh: 廓性剛褊，被詰治峻急，詔書未至，以憤死。

translations.literal: Kuo's nature was harsh and narrow; subjected to severe interrogation, before the edict arrived he died of anger.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was harsh and narrow by nature; under severe interrogation, before the edict of exoneration arrived he died of anger.

sentences.zh: 上聞，甚追悼之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he greatly mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard he deeply mourned him.

sentences.zh: 復驗仁甫所訴，多無實狀，免韶官，貶仁甫商州長史，贈廓右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Re-investigating Renpu's accusations, most had no factual basis; Shao was removed from office, Renpu demoted to senior recorder of Shang Prefecture, and Kuo posthumously granted Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Re-investigating Renpu's accusations, most had no factual basis; Shao was removed from office, Renpu demoted to senior recorder of Shang Prefecture, and Kuo was posthumously granted Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 錄其子丘賀為奉禮郎，始十歲。

translations.literal: His son Qiuhuo was enrolled as Court Gentleman for Ceremonies, only ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiuhuo was enrolled as Court Gentleman for Ceremonies at only ten years of age.

sentences.zh: 上猶念廓不已，又詔削仁甫名籍，配隸商州。

translations.literal: The emperor still thought of Kuo unceasingly and again ordered Renpu's name struck from the registers and assigned to penal service in Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought of Kuo unceasingly and again ordered Renpu's name struck from the registers and assigned to penal service in Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 樊知古

translations.literal: Fan Zhigu
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhigu

sentences.zh: 樊知古，字仲師，其先京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhigu, style name Zhongshi; his ancestors were men of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhigu, whose style name was Zhongshi, was descended from men of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖偁，濮州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Cheng was Shaan Prefecture Revenue Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Cheng was Revenue Registrar of Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖知諭，事吳為金壇令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhiyu served Wu as magistrate of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhiyu served Wu as magistrate of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 父潛，事李景，任漢陽、石埭二縣令，因家池州。

translations.literal: His father Qian served Li Jing as magistrate of Hanyang and Shidai counties and thus made his home in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian served Li Jing as magistrate of Hanyang and Shidai and made his home in Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 知古嘗舉進士不第，遂謀北歸，乃漁釣采石江上數月，乘小舟載絲繩，維南岸，疾棹抵北岸，以度江之廣狹。

translations.literal: Zhigu once took the jinshi examination but did not pass; then he plotted to go north; he fished on the Caishi River for several months; riding a small boat he carried silk cord, moored at the south bank, rowed swiftly to the north bank to measure the river's width.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu once failed the jinshi examination and then plotted to go north; he fished on the Caishi River for several months, and in a small boat carried silk cord, moored at the south bank, and rowed swiftly to the north bank to measure the river's width.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，詣闕上書，言江南可取狀，以求進用。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he came to court and memorialized on the form in which Jiangnan could be taken, seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao he came to court and memorialized describing how Jiangnan could be taken, seeking advancement.

sentences.zh: 太祖令送學士院試，賜本科及第，解褐舒州軍事推官。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered him sent to the Academy for examination; he was granted rank equal to jinshi graduates and began service as investigating censor of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu ordered him examined at the Academy; he was granted rank equal to a jinshi graduate and began service as investigating censor of Shu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘗啟於上，言老母親屬數十口在江南，恐為李煜所害，願迎至治所。

translations.literal: He once reported to the emperor that several dozen close kin remained in Jiangnan and feared harm from Li Yu, and wished them brought to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He once reported that several dozen close kin remained in Jiangnan and feared harm from Li Yu, and asked that they be brought to his post.

sentences.zh: 即詔煜令遣之。

translations.literal: An edict at once ordered Yu to send them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict at once ordered Yu to send them.

sentences.zh: 煜方聞命，即厚給齎裝，護送至境上。

translations.literal: Yu had just received the order and at once generously provided travel funds and escorted them to the border.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had just received the order and at once generously provided travel funds and escorted them to the border.

sentences.zh: 七年，召拜太子右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 會王師征江表，知古為鄉導，下池州。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned on the Jiang table, Zhigu served as local guide and took Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned south of the Yangtze, Zhigu served as local guide and took Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，以知古領州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zhigu was put in charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Zhigu was put in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，州民保險為寇，知古擊之，連拔三砦，擒其魁以獻，餘皆潰散。

translations.literal: Earlier the prefectural people had relied on terrain for banditry; Zhigu attacked them, in succession took three stockades, captured their chieftain and presented him, and the rest all fled and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the people had relied on terrain for banditry; Zhigu attacked them, took three stockades in succession, captured their chieftain and presented him, and the rest fled and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 方議南征，命高品石全振往湖南造黃黑龍船，以大艦載巨竹縆，自荊南而下，遣八作使郝守濬等率丁匠營之。

translations.literal: When the southern campaign was being discussed, high-ranking officer Shi Quanzhen was sent to Hunan to build yellow and black dragon boats; great ships carried huge bamboo cables from Jingnan downstream; Eight Works Commissioner Hao Shoujun and others led corvée craftsmen to construct them.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern campaign was being discussed, high-ranking officer Shi Quanzhen was sent to Hunan to build yellow and black dragon boats; great ships carried huge bamboo cables downstream from Jingnan, and Eight Works Commissioner Hao Shoujun and others led corvée craftsmen to build them.

sentences.zh: 議者以謂江濤險壯，恐不能就，乃於石碑口試造之，移至采石，三日橋成，不差尺寸，從知古之請也。

translations.literal: Opinion held that the river's waves were fierce and feared it could not be done; therefore at Shibei Ford a trial bridge was built, moved to Caishi, and completed in three days without error in measurement—this followed Zhigu's request.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion held that the river's waves were too fierce, but a trial bridge was built at Shibei Ford, moved to Caishi, and completed in three days without error in measurement—following Zhigu's plan.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，擢拜侍御史，令乘傳按行江南諸州，詢訪利民，復命知江南東路轉運事。

translations.literal: When Jinling was pacified he was promoted to Attending Censor and ordered to travel by post inspecting the Jiangnan prefectures, inquiring what benefited the people; on return he was again ordered to manage Jiangnan East Circuit transport affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling was pacified he was promoted to Attending Censor and ordered to travel by post through the Jiangnan prefectures inquiring what benefited the people; on his return he was again ordered to manage Jiangnan East Circuit transport affairs.

sentences.zh: 數日，改授江南轉運使，賜錢一百萬。

translations.literal: Several days later he was changed to Jiangnan transport commissioner and granted a million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was made Jiangnan transport commissioner and granted a million cash.

sentences.zh: 先是，江南諸州官市茶十分之八，復徵其餘分，然後給符聽其所往，商人苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jiangnan prefectures in official tea purchases took eight-tenths and then levied the remaining portion again before issuing permits for where merchants might go; merchants suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jiangnan prefectures in official tea purchases took eight-tenths and then levied the remainder again before issuing permits for where merchants might go, to the merchants' great distress.

sentences.zh: 知古請蠲其稅，仍差增所市之直，以便於民。

translations.literal: Zhigu requested remission of that tax and also ordered increased purchase prices to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu asked that the tax be remitted and purchase prices increased to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 江南舊用鐵錢，十當銅錢之一，物價翔踴，民不便，知古亦奏罷之。

translations.literal: Jiangnan formerly used iron cash, ten pieces equaling one copper cash; prices soared and the people found it inconvenient; Zhigu also memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan had used iron cash at ten to one copper cash, prices soared, and the people suffered; Zhigu also memorialized to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 先是，李煜用兵，權宜調斂，知古悉奏為常額。

translations.literal: Earlier when Li Yu used troops, exactions were levied as expedients; Zhigu memorialized that all be made regular quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier when Li Yu raised troops, expedient levies had been imposed; Zhigu memorialized that all be made standing quotas.

sentences.zh: 豫章洪氏嘗掌昇州榷酤，逋鐵錢數百萬。

translations.literal: The Hong clan of Yuzhang had once managed the Shengzhou liquor monopoly and owed several million in iron cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong clan of Yuzhang had once managed the Shengzhou liquor monopoly and owed several million in iron cash.

sentences.zh: 至是，知古挾微時嘗辱於洪氏，責償銅錢以快意。

translations.literal: By then Zhigu, bearing a slight from the Hong clan in his youth, demanded repayment in copper cash to satisfy himself.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhigu, remembering a slight from the Hong clan in his youth, demanded repayment in copper cash to satisfy himself.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，授庫部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Stores.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong acceded he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Stores.

sentences.zh: 召歸，換金紫，賜錢百萬，命為京西北路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was recalled, exchanged gold and purple, granted a million cash, and made transport commissioner of the Capital Northwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, granted gold and purple insignia and a million cash, and made transport commissioner of the Capital Northwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，加虞部郎中，就改知邠州，移鳳翔府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he was added Parks Director and then changed to govern Bin Prefecture and transferred to Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo he was made Parks Director, then prefect of Bin, then transferred to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 入為鹽鐵判官，出領荊湖轉運使。

translations.literal: He entered as Salt and Iron Auditor and went out to head Jinghu transport.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Salt and Iron Auditor and went out to head Jinghu transport.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，遷比部郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Accounts Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會河朔用兵，分諸郡為兩路，以給漕輓。

translations.literal: When troops were used in Hebei, the prefectures were divided into two circuits to supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: When troops were mobilized in Hebei the prefectures were divided into two circuits to supply transport.

sentences.zh: 遷知古為東路轉運使，遷駕部郎中，賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Zhigu was transferred to be Eastern Circuit transport commissioner and promoted to Carriages Director, granted five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu was made Eastern Circuit transport commissioner and promoted to Director in the Ministry of Carriages, with a grant of five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 知古本名若水，字叔清，因召見，上問之曰：「卿名出何書？」

translations.literal: Zhigu's original name was Ruoshui, style name Shuqing; because of a summons to audience the emperor asked him: From what book does your name come?
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu's original name was Ruoshui, style name Shuqing; at an audience the emperor asked, From what book does your name come?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「唐尚書右丞倪若水亮直，臣竊慕之。」

translations.literal: He replied: Tang Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Ni Ruoshui was upright; your servant secretly admires him.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, Tang Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Ni Ruoshui was upright; your servant secretly admires him.

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「可改名『知古』」。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: You may change your name to Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, You may change your name to Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 知古頓首奉詔。

translations.literal: Zhigu bowed his head and accepted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu bowed and accepted the edict.

sentences.zh: 倪若水實名「若冰」，知古學淺，妄引以對，人皆笑之。

translations.literal: Ni Ruoshui's actual name was Ruobing; Zhigu's learning was shallow and he falsely cited him in reply; everyone laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Ruoshui's actual name was Ruobing; Zhigu's learning was shallow and he cited the wrong name in reply, to everyone's amusement.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷右諫議大夫、河北東西路都轉運使，賜白金千兩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was transferred to Right Remonstrating Grandee and overall transport commissioner of Hebei East and West circuits, granted a thousand taels of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he was made Right Remonstrating Grandee and overall transport commissioner of Hebei East and West circuits, with a grant of a thousand taels of white gold.

sentences.zh: 兩路各置轉運副使，都轉運使之名自知古始。

translations.literal: Each circuit was given a deputy transport commissioner; the title of overall transport commissioner began with Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit was given a deputy transport commissioner; the title of overall transport commissioner began with Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔加河北西路招置營田使。

translations.literal: In the second year an edict added him as Hebei West Circuit commissioner for establishing military farms.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict added him as Hebei West Circuit commissioner for establishing military farms.

sentences.zh: 奏請修城木五百餘萬、牛革三百萬。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting more than five million units of timber for wall repair and three million of ox hides.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting more than five million units of timber for wall repair and three million ox hides.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「萬里長城豈在於此？

translations.literal: The emperor said: Is the ten-thousand-li Great Wall really in this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, Is the ten-thousand-li Great Wall really built of this?

sentences.zh: 自古匈奴、黃河，互為中國之患。

translations.literal: From antiquity the Xiongnu and the Yellow River have each been a calamity to China.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the northern nomads and the Yellow River have each been a calamity to China.

sentences.zh: 朕自即位以來，或疆埸無事，則有修築圩堤之役。

translations.literal: Since I acceded, when the borders are quiet there is work on dikes and embankments.
translations.idiomatic: Since I acceded, when the borders are quiet there is work on dikes and embankments.

sentences.zh: 近者邊烽稍警，則黃河安流無害，此蓋天意更迭垂戒，常令惕厲。

translations.literal: Recently the frontier beacons have been somewhat alarming, yet the Yellow River flows peacefully without harm—this is perhaps Heaven's alternating admonition, constantly to keep us vigilant.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the frontier beacons have been somewhat alarming, yet the Yellow River flows peacefully without harm—perhaps Heaven's alternating admonition to keep us vigilant.

sentences.zh: 然而預備不虞，古之善教，深溝高壘，亦王公設險之義也。

translations.literal: Yet preparedness against the unforeseen is the good teaching of antiquity; deep moats and high ramparts are also the meaning of kings and dukes establishing defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet preparedness against the unforeseen is the good teaching of antiquity; deep moats and high ramparts are also what kings and dukes mean by establishing defenses.

sentences.zh: 所請過當，不亦重困吾民乎？」

translations.literal: Your request is excessive—will it not heavily burden our people?
translations.idiomatic: Your request is excessive—will it not heavily burden our people?

sentences.zh: 乃詔有司量以官物給之。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the relevant offices to measure and supply government goods.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the relevant offices to measure and supply government goods.

sentences.zh: 會度支使李惟清上言河北軍儲無備，請發河南十七軍州轉粟以赴。

translations.literal: When Revenue Commissioner Li Weiqing memorialized that Hebei army stores were unprepared and requested grain be transported from seventeen armies and prefectures of Henan,
translations.idiomatic: When Revenue Commissioner Li Weiqing memorialized that Hebei army stores were unprepared and requested grain transported from seventeen armies and prefectures of Henan,

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「農事方殷，豈可更興此役？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: Agricultural work is just at its height—how can we launch this labor again?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, Agricultural work is at its height—how can we launch this labor again?

sentences.zh: 惟清固以為請，上遣左正言馮拯乘傳與知古計之。

translations.literal: Weiqing firmly pressed his request; the emperor sent Left Rectifier Feng Zheng by post to plan with Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing firmly pressed his request; the emperor sent Left Rectifier Feng Zheng by post to plan with Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 知古即言：「河北軍儲可以均濟足，俟農隙令民轉餉。」

translations.literal: Zhigu at once said: Hebei army stores can be balanced and made sufficient; wait until a break in farming and order the people to transport provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu at once said, Hebei army stores can be balanced and made sufficient; wait until a break in farming and order the people to transport provisions.

sentences.zh: 拯復命，太宗曰：「不細籌之，則民果受弊矣。」

translations.literal: Zheng returned to report; Taizong said: Without careful planning the people would indeed have suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng returned to report; Taizong said, Without careful planning the people would indeed have suffered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入朝奏事稱旨，拜給事中。

translations.literal: Before long, coming to court to memorialize and pleasing the emperor, he was appointed Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, memorializing at court to the emperor's satisfaction, he was appointed Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 俄為戶部使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Revenue Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Revenue Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 知古有才力，累任轉運使，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: Zhigu had talent and ability; he repeatedly served as transport commissioner and won great reputation at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu was talented and capable; he repeatedly served as transport commissioner and won great reputation.

sentences.zh: 及在戶部，頻以職事不治，詔書切責，名益減。

translations.literal: When in the Revenue Ministry he frequently failed in his duties; edicts sternly rebuked him and his reputation declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the Revenue Ministry he frequently failed in his duties; edicts sternly rebuked him and his reputation declined.

sentences.zh: 素與陳恕親善，恕時參知政事，太宗言及計司事有乖違者，恕具以告。

translations.literal: He had long been friendly with Chen Shu; Shu was then Associate Administrator; when Taizong spoke of Revenue Office matters that were awry, Shu told him all.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Chen Shu; Shu was then Associate Administrator, and when Taizong spoke of Revenue Office irregularities Shu told Zhigu everything.

sentences.zh: 後因奏事，知古遂自解。

translations.literal: Later when memorializing at court, Zhigu explained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later when memorializing at court Zhigu explained himself.

sentences.zh: 上問：「從何得知？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: How did you learn of it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, How did you learn of it?

sentences.zh: 曰：「陳恕告臣。」

translations.literal: He said: Chen Shu told your servant.
translations.idiomatic: He said, Chen Shu told me.

sentences.zh: 上怒恕泄禁中語，且嫉知古輕侻，故兩罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that Shu had leaked palace words and also resented Zhigu's flippancy, and therefore dismissed both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry that Shu had leaked palace secrets and resented Zhigu's flippancy, and dismissed both.

sentences.zh: 出知古知梓州，未至，改西川轉運使。

translations.literal: Zhigu was sent out to govern Zizhou; before he arrived he was changed to Western Chuan transport commissioner.
