translations.idiomatic: Zhigu was sent out as prefect of Zizhou; before he arrived he was changed to Western Chuan transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 知古自以嘗任三司使，一旦掌漕運劍外，鬱鬱不得志，常稱足疾，未嘗按行郡縣。

translations.literal: Zhigu thought that having once been Revenue Commissioner, to hold transport of sword-land all at once left him depressed and discontent; he often claimed foot ailment and never inspected prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu thought that having once been Revenue Commissioner, to hold transport of the sword regions alone left him depressed; he often claimed foot ailments and never inspected prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 蜀中富饒，羅紈錦綺等物甲天下，言事者競商榷功利。

translations.literal: Shu was rich; silk, gauze, brocade, and the like were foremost under Heaven; memorialists competed to discuss profit.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was rich; silk, gauze, and brocade were foremost under Heaven, and memorialists competed to discuss profit.

sentences.zh: 又土狹民稠，耕種不足給，由是兼並者益糴賤販貴以規利。

translations.literal: The land was narrow and the people numerous; farming could not fully supply them, and therefore those who combined holdings bought cheap and sold dear for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The land was narrow and the people numerous; farming could not fully supply them, and magnates bought cheap and sold dear for profit.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，青城縣民王小波聚眾為亂，謂其眾曰：「吾疾貧富不均，今為汝輩均之。」

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era Qingcheng county man Wang Xiaobo gathered a crowd in rebellion, telling his followers: I hate that rich and poor are not equal; now I will equalize them for you.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunhua era Wang Xiaobo of Qingcheng county gathered a crowd in rebellion, telling his followers, I hate that rich and poor are not equal; now I will equalize them for you.

sentences.zh: 附者益眾，遂攻陷青城縣，掠彭山，殺其令齊元振。

translations.literal: Those who joined grew ever more numerous; they then took Qingcheng county, plundered Pengshan, and killed its magistrate Qi Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who joined grew ever more numerous; they then took Qingcheng, plundered Pengshan, and killed its magistrate Qi Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 巡檢使張玘與鬥於江源縣，射小波，中其額，旋病創死，玘亦被殺。

translations.literal: Inspector Zhang Qi fought them at Jiangyuan county; he shot Xiaobo in the forehead; soon he died of the wound, and Qi was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zhang Qi fought them at Jiangyuan; he shot Xiaobo in the forehead; soon Xiaobo died of the wound, and Qi was also killed.

sentences.zh: 眾遂推小波妻弟李順為帥。

translations.literal: The crowd then made Xiaobo's brother-in-law Li Shun commander.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd then made Xiaobo's brother-in-law Li Shun commander.

sentences.zh: 初，小波黨與裁百人，州縣失於備禦，故所在蜂起，至萬餘人。

translations.literal: At first Xiaobo's party numbered barely a hundred; prefectures and counties failed in defense, and therefore uprisings flared everywhere until they exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiaobo's party numbered barely a hundred; prefectures and counties failed in defense, and uprisings flared everywhere until they exceeded ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 攻蜀州，殺監軍王亮及官吏十餘人。

translations.literal: They attacked Shu Prefecture and killed military inspector Wang Liang and more than ten officials.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Shu Prefecture and killed military inspector Wang Liang and more than ten officials.

sentences.zh: 陷邛州，害知州桑保紳、通判王從式及諸僚吏，逐都巡檢使郭允能。

translations.literal: They took Qiong Prefecture, killed prefect Sang Baoshen, administrative prefect Wang Congshi, and all subordinate officials, and drove off chief inspector Guo Yunneng.
translations.idiomatic: They took Qiong Prefecture, killed prefect Sang Baoshen, administrative prefect Wang Congshi, and all subordinate officials, and drove off chief inspector Guo Yunneng.

sentences.zh: 允能率麾下與戰新津江口，為賊所殺，同巡檢、殿直毛儼徒步以身免。

translations.literal: Yunneng led his subordinates to fight at the Xinjin river mouth and was killed by the bandits; fellow inspector and palace attendant Mao Yan escaped on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Yunneng led his subordinates to fight at the Xinjin river mouth and was killed; fellow inspector and palace attendant Mao Yan escaped on foot.

sentences.zh: 賊勢益張，眾至數萬人，陷永康軍、雙流、新津、溫江、郫縣，縱火大掠，留其黨守之。

translations.literal: The bandits' power grew greater; the crowd reached tens of thousands; they took Yongkang Army, Shuangliu, Xinjin, Wenjiang, and Pixian, set great fires and plundered widely, and left their party to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits grew stronger until tens of thousands took Yongkang Army, Shuangliu, Xinjin, Wenjiang, and Pixian, set great fires and plundered widely, and left their party to hold them.

sentences.zh: 往攻成都，燒西郭門，不利，引去。

translations.literal: They went to attack Chengdu, burned the western gate, met ill fortune, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They went to attack Chengdu, burned the western gate, met ill fortune, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 陷漢州、彭州，旋陷成都。

translations.literal: They took Han and Peng prefectures, then soon took Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: They took Han and Peng prefectures, then soon took Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 時已詔知梓州、右諫議大夫張雍代知古為轉運使。

translations.literal: By then an edict had appointed Zhang Yong, who was governing Zizhou as Right Remonstrating Grandee, to replace Zhigu as transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: By then an edict had appointed Zhang Yong, governing Zizhou as Right Remonstrating Grandee, to replace Zhigu as transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 雍未至，知古與知府郭載及屬官走東川。

translations.literal: Yong had not yet arrived; Zhigu fled east with prefect Guo Zai and subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had not yet arrived; Zhigu fled east with prefect Guo Zai and subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 詔復令掌兩川漕運。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered him to manage Two Chuan transport.
translations.idiomatic: An edict again ordered him to manage Two Chuan transport.

sentences.zh: 知古具伏擅離所部，制置無狀，上特宥之，以本官出知均州。

translations.literal: Zhigu fully confessed leaving his post without authorization and inept disposition; the emperor specially pardoned him and sent him out as prefect of Jun with his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu fully confessed leaving his post without authorization and inept leadership; the emperor specially pardoned him and sent him out as prefect of Jun with his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 視事旬日，憂悸卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: After ten days in office he died of anxiety, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days in office he died of anxiety, at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 上猶嗟憫，賜其子漢公同學究出身。

translations.literal: The emperor still sighed in pity and granted his son Hangong passage of the classicist examination.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still sighed in pity and granted his son Hangong passage of the classicist examination.

sentences.zh: 知古明俊有吏幹，辭辨捷給，及任西川，不能弭盜而逃，雖獲宥，終以慙死云。

translations.literal: Zhigu was bright and capable in administrative matters, quick and ready in debate; yet in Western Chuan he could not suppress bandits and fled; though pardoned, he finally died of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu was bright and capable, quick in debate; yet in Western Chuan he could not suppress bandits and fled; though pardoned, he finally died of shame.

sentences.zh: 郭載

translations.literal: Guo Zai
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zai

translations.literal: 〈Appendix〉
translations.idiomatic: (Appendix)

sentences.zh: 郭載，字咸熙，開封浚儀人。

translations.literal: Guo Zai, style name Xianxi, was a man of Junyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zai, whose style name was Xianxi, came from Junyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父暉，右監門衛將軍、義州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Hui was General of the Right Palace Gate Guards and prefect of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was General of the Right Palace Gate Guards and prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 載蔭為右班殿直，累遷供奉官、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Through privilege Zai was made Right Guard Attendant and was successively promoted to Palace Attendant and Attendant of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Through privilege Zai was made Right Guard Attendant and rose to Palace Attendant and Attendant of the Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，提舉西川兵馬捕盜事，太宗賜鞍馬、器械、銀錢以遣之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was commissioned to raise Western Chuan troops to capture bandits; Taizong granted saddle horses, weapons, silver, and cash to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi he was commissioned to raise Western Chuan troops to capture bandits; Taizong granted saddle horses, weapons, silver, and cash to send him off.

sentences.zh: 四年，以積勞加崇儀副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, for accumulated merit he was added Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, for accumulated merit he was made Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 召還，上言：「川、峽富人俗多贅婿，死則與其子均分其財，故貧者多。」

translations.literal: When recalled he memorialized: In Chuan and Xia the custom among the rich is often uxorilocal marriage; when the father dies the property is divided equally with the son, and therefore many are poor.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled he memorialized, In Chuan and Xia the rich often practice uxorilocal marriage; when the father dies property is divided equally with the son, and therefore many are poor.

sentences.zh: 詔禁之。

translations.literal: An edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade it.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，擢引進副使、知天雄軍，入同勾當三班，出知秦州兼沿邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong he was promoted to Vice Commissioner for Introduction and made to govern Tianxiong Army; he entered to jointly manage the Three Classes and went out as prefect of Qin with concurrent frontier chief inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Duangong he was promoted to Vice Commissioner for Introduction and prefect of Tianxiong; he entered to jointly manage the Three Classes and went out as prefect of Qin with concurrent frontier chief inspector.

sentences.zh: 先是，巡邊者多領兵騎以威戎人，所至頗煩苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier those who inspected the frontier often led cavalry to overawe the barbarians, and wherever they went caused considerable hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier frontier inspectors often led cavalry to overawe the barbarians and caused considerable hardship wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 載悉減去，戎人感悅。

translations.literal: Zai reduced them all; the barbarians were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zai reduced them all; the barbarians were moved and pleased.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門使，改知成都府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Upper Palace Gate Commissioner and changed to govern Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Western Upper Palace Gate Commissioner and made prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 載在天雄軍，屢奏市糴朝臣段獻可、馮侃等所市粗惡，軍人皆曰：「此物安可充食？」

translations.literal: At Tianxiong Army Zai repeatedly memorialized that court ministers Duan Xianke and Feng Kan's purchases were coarse and inferior; the soldiers all said: How can this stuff serve as food?
translations.idiomatic: At Tianxiong Army Zai repeatedly memorialized that court ministers Duan Xianke and Feng Kan's purchases were coarse and inferior; the soldiers all said, How can this stuff serve as food?

sentences.zh: 太宗頗疑，使覆驗之，及報，與戴奏同。

translations.literal: Taizu was quite suspicious and ordered re-investigation; when the report came it matched Zai's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was quite suspicious and ordered re-investigation; when the report came it matched Zai's memorial.

sentences.zh: 獻可等皆坐削官，仍令填償。

translations.literal: Xianke and the others were all punished by reduction of rank and ordered to make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke and the others were all reduced in rank and ordered to make restitution.

sentences.zh: 及載受代，獻可等所市皆支畢，復有羨數。

translations.literal: When Zai was relieved, what Xianke and the others had purchased was all paid out and there was still a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai was relieved, what Xianke and the others had purchased was all paid out and there was still a surplus.

sentences.zh: 三司判勾馮拯以聞，太宗召度支使魏羽詰之。

translations.literal: Three Departments auditor Feng Zheng reported this; Taizong summoned Revenue Commissioner Wei Yu to question him.
translations.idiomatic: Three Departments auditor Feng Zheng reported this; Taizong summoned Revenue Commissioner Wei Yu to question him.

sentences.zh: 羽曰：「獻可等所市不至粗惡，亦無欠數。

translations.literal: Yu said: What Xianke and the others purchased was not to the point of coarse inferiority, nor was there any shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, What Xianke and the others purchased was not coarse or inferior, nor was there any shortage.

sentences.zh: 臣與侃親舊，是以未敢白。」

translations.literal: Your servant is intimate with Kan and therefore did not dare report it.
translations.idiomatic: I am intimate with Kan and therefore did not dare report it.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「此公事爾，何用畏避？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: This is a public matter—why use evasion?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, This is a public matter—why evade it?

sentences.zh: 因詔宰相謂曰：「此乃郭載力奏，朕累與卿等議，皆云有實。

translations.literal: He then told the chancellor: This was vigorously memorialized by Guo Zai; I repeatedly discussed it with you all and you said there were facts.
translations.idiomatic: He then told the chancellor, This was vigorously memorialized by Guo Zai; I repeatedly discussed it with you all and you said there were facts.

sentences.zh: 今支畢，頗有羨餘，軍士復無詞訴。

translations.literal: Now it is all paid out and there is quite a surplus; the soldiers again have no complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is all paid out with quite a surplus, and the soldiers again have no complaints.

sentences.zh: 郭載，朕向以純誠待之，何為矯誣及此？

translations.literal: Guo Zai—I have always treated him with pure sincerity; why does he fabricate and deceive to this extent?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zai—I have always treated him with pure sincerity; why does he fabricate and deceive to this extent?

sentences.zh: 然已委西川，俟還日別當詰責。」

translations.literal: Yet he has already been assigned to Western Chuan; wait until he returns and then deal with the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has already been assigned to Western Chuan; wait until he returns and then deal with the matter.

sentences.zh: 於是獻可等悉復官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xianke and the others were all restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xianke and the others were all restored to office.

sentences.zh: 載行至梓州，時李順已構亂，有日者潛告載曰：「益州必陷，公往當受禍，少留數日可免。」

translations.literal: When Zai reached Zizhou, Li Shun had already raised rebellion; a diviner secretly told Zai: Yizhou will surely fall; if you go you will suffer disaster; stay a few days and you can escape.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai reached Zizhou, Li Shun had already raised rebellion; a diviner secretly told Zai, Yizhou will surely fall; if you go you will suffer disaster; stay a few days and you can escape.

sentences.zh: 載怒曰：「吾受詔領方面，阽危之際，豈敢遷延邪？」

translations.literal: Zai angrily said: I received an edict to govern a region; at a moment of peril how dare I delay?
translations.idiomatic: Zai angrily said, I received an edict to govern a region; at a moment of peril how dare I delay?

sentences.zh: 即日入成都。

translations.literal: That same day he entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 順兵攻城益急，不能拒守，乃與樊知古率僚屬斬關出，以餘眾由梓州趨劍門，隨招安使王繼恩統兵討順，平之，復入成都。

translations.literal: Shun's troops pressed the siege ever tighter; unable to defend, he together with Fan Zhigu led subordinates to cut through the gate and flee; with the remaining troops they went by Zizhou toward Jianmen, followed Pacification Commissioner Wang Jien who commanded troops to suppress Shun and pacify him, then re-entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's troops pressed the siege ever tighter; unable to defend, he with Fan Zhigu led subordinates to cut through the gate and flee; with the remaining troops they went by Zizhou toward Jianmen, followed Pacification Commissioner Wang Jien who commanded troops to suppress Shun, then re-entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 月餘，憂患成病，卒，年四十。

translations.literal: After more than a month, worry and illness brought death, aged forty.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month, worry and illness brought death, at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 載前在蜀，頗能為民除害，故蜀民悅之。

translations.literal: Earlier in Shu Zai had been quite able to remove harm for the people, and therefore the people of Shu were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Shu Zai had been quite able to remove harm for the people, and the people of Shu were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 再至成都，即值兵亂，及隨繼恩平賊，亦有所全濟。

translations.literal: When he came again to Chengdu he immediately met military chaos; when he followed Jien to pacify the bandits he also saved many.
translations.idiomatic: When he came again to Chengdu he immediately met military chaos; when he followed Jien to pacify the bandits he also saved many.

sentences.zh: 故其死也，成都人多歎惜之。

translations.literal: Therefore at his death many in Chengdu sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at his death many in Chengdu sighed in regret.

sentences.zh: 臧丙，字夢壽，大名人。

translations.literal: Zang Bing, style name Mengshou, was a man of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Bing, whose style name was Mengshou, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 弱冠好學。

translations.literal: In his youth he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初舉進士，解褐大理評事，通判大寧監，官課民煮井為鹽，丙職兼總其事。

translations.literal: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he passed the jinshi examination, took office as Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review, and served as vice-prefect of the Daning Supervisorate; the government levied the people to boil wells for salt, and Bing's duties included overseeing the matter in general.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and vice-prefect of the Daning Supervisorate; the state taxed the people for well-salt production, and Bing was charged with overseeing it.

sentences.zh: 先是，官給錢市薪，吏多侵牟，至歲課不充，坐械繫者常數十百人。

translations.literal: Previously the government supplied money to buy fuelwood; clerks often extorted and profited, until the annual quota could not be met, and those held in shackles for it often numbered scores or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Before his arrival the government paid out money for fuelwood, but clerks often skimmed and extorted until the yearly quota fell short, and dozens or hundreds were regularly shackled for it.

sentences.zh: 丙至，召井戶面付以錢，既而市薪山積，歲鹽致有羨數。

translations.literal: When Bing arrived, he summoned the well households and paid them the money face to face; before long fuelwood was piled mountain-high, and the annual salt yield had a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing took over, he summoned the well households and paid them in person; soon fuelwood was piled high, and the year's salt output showed a surplus.

sentences.zh: 太宗平晉陽，以丙為右贊善大夫、知遼州。

translations.literal: When Taizong pacified Jinyang, he appointed Bing Right Gentlemen for Promoting Goodness and prefect of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong pacified Jinyang, he made Bing Right Gentlemen for Promoting Goodness and prefect of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 丙素剛果，有吏幹。

translations.literal: Bing had always been firm and resolute, with administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was by nature firm and decisive and had a gift for administration.

sentences.zh: 會同年生馮汝士以秘書丞知石州，與監軍不協，一夕剚刃於腹而死，事可疑。

translations.literal: It happened that his fellow examination-year graduate Feng Rushi, serving as Secretary of the Secretariat and governing Shizhou, did not get along with the army supervisor; one night he stabbed a blade into his belly and died—the matter was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow jinshi of the same year, Feng Rushi, was serving as Secretary of the Secretariat and governing Shizhou; he fell out with the army supervisor, and one night died with a blade thrust into his belly—a suspicious case.

sentences.zh: 丙上疏言汝士死非自殺，乞按治。

translations.literal: Bing submitted a memorial saying Ruoshi's death was not suicide, and requested an investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Bing memorialized that Ruoshi had not killed himself and asked that the matter be investigated.

sentences.zh: 上覽奏驚駭，即遣使鞫之，召丙問狀。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and was startled; he immediately sent an envoy to interrogate the case and summoned Bing to inquire into the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with alarm, immediately sent an envoy to investigate, and summoned Bing to question him about the facts.

sentences.zh: 丙曰：「汝士居牧守之任，不聞有私罪，而言自殺，若使冤死不明，不加宿直者以罪，今後書生不能治邊郡矣。」

translations.literal: Bing said: "Ruoshi held the post of regional governor; one never heard he had private crimes, yet they say he killed himself. If an unjust death remains unclear and the night-duty officer is not punished, hereafter scholars will not be able to govern border prefectures."
translations.idiomatic: Bing said, "Ruoshi held a prefectural governorship; no private offense was ever heard against him, yet they call it suicide. If a wrongful death is left unexplained and the officer on night watch is not punished, hereafter no scholar will dare govern a frontier prefecture."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其直，改著作郎，俄遷右拾遺、直史館。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his frankness, changed his post to Compiler, and soon promoted him to Right Reminder and Historiographer in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his bluntness, made him Compiler, and soon promoted him to Right Reminder and Historiographer in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 加工部員外郎，充河東轉運使，俄兼本路營田使。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, appointed Transport Commissioner for Hedong, and soon also concurrently Commissioner for Military Colonies on that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, appointed Hedong transport commissioner, and soon also military-colony commissioner for that circuit.

sentences.zh: 代歸，授戶部郎中、同知審官院。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Associate Manager of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and associate manager of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方以九寺亞列為重，改司農少卿。

translations.literal: The court at the time regarded the nine directorates as ranked in parallel pairs as important; he was changed to Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The court then valued the nine directorates as paired in parallel rank; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，拜右諫議大夫，出知江陵府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was appointed Right Remonstrating Censor and went out to serve as prefect of Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was made Right Remonstrating Censor and sent out as prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，疾。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，遣中使及尚醫馳往視之，逾月卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he sent a palace envoy and the Imperial Physician posthaste to attend him; after more than a month he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he sent a palace envoy and the imperial physician posthaste to see him; after more than a month he died, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 上軫悼之，以其子待用為四門助教。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him deeply and appointed his son Daiyong as Instructor at the Four Gates Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved for him and appointed his son Daiyong Instructor at the Four Gates Academy.

sentences.zh: 丙舊名愚，字仲回。

translations.literal: Bing's original name was Yu, courtesy name Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had originally been named Yu, with the courtesy name Zhonghui.

sentences.zh: 既孤，常夢其父召丙偶立於庭，向空指曰：「老人星見矣。」

translations.literal: After he was orphaned, he often dreamed his father summoned Bing to stand paired in the courtyard, pointed toward the sky and said: "The Old Man Star has appeared."
translations.idiomatic: After he was orphaned he often dreamed that his father called Bing to stand beside him in the courtyard, pointed at the sky, and said, "The Old Man Star has appeared."

sentences.zh: 丙仰視之，黃明潤大，因望而拜。

translations.literal: Bing looked up; it was yellow, bright, lustrous, and large, and he therefore gazed up and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Bing looked up; it was yellow, bright, lustrous, and large, and he gazed up and bowed.

sentences.zh: 既寤，私喜曰：「吉祥也。」

translations.literal: When he awoke, he said privately with joy: "An auspicious sign."
translations.idiomatic: When he awoke he said privately with delight, "An auspicious omen."

sentences.zh: 以壽星出丙入丁，乃改名焉，至是無驗。

translations.literal: Because the longevity star emerged in the geng direction and entered the ding direction, he thereupon changed his name—yet in the end it was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Because the longevity star appeared in geng and entered ding, he changed his name accordingly—but in the end the omen was not fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 丙於禮不當更名，古人戒數占夢，無妄喜也。

translations.literal: By ritual Bing ought not to have changed his name; the ancients warned against frequent divination by dreams—one ought not rejoice without cause.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual Bing should not have changed his name; the ancients warned against repeated dream-divination—one must not rejoice without reason.

sentences.zh: 待用歷金部郎中、東染院使、賀州刺史。

translations.literal: Daiyong served successively as Vice Director in the Ministry of Finance, Commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Court, and prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Daiyong served in turn as Vice Director in the Ministry of Finance, commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Court, and prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 次子列進士及第，至太常丞。

translations.literal: His second son Lie passed the jinshi examination and rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Lie passed the jinshi examination and rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 徐休復

translations.literal: Xu Xiufu
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiufu

sentences.zh: 徐休復，字廣初，濮州鄄城人。

translations.literal: Xu Xiufu, courtesy name Guangchu, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiufu, whose courtesy name was Guangchu, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初舉進士，解褐大理評事、通判。

translations.literal: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he passed the jinshi examination and took office as Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi and entered service as Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 轉運使薦其材，代歸，授太子右贊善大夫，改著作郎、直史館，賜緋魚，遷左拾遺。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner recommended his talent; when his term ended he was appointed Right Gentlemen for Promoting Goodness to the Heir Apparent, changed to Compiler and Historiographer in the History Office, granted crimson robe and fish tally, and promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner recommended his ability; when his term ended he was made Right Gentlemen for Promoting Goodness to the Heir Apparent, then Compiler and Historiographer in the History Office, granted crimson robe and fish tally, and promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 六年，加右補闕，充兩浙東北路轉運副使，移知明州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was given the additional title of Right Supplements-the-Omissions, appointed Deputy Transport Commissioner for the Eastern and Northern Two Zhe Circuits, and transferred to govern Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given the additional title of Right Supplements-the-Omissions, made deputy transport commissioner of the Eastern and Northern Two Zhe circuits, and transferred to govern Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，被召赴闕，明年，授庫部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: In autumn of the seventh year he was summoned to court; the next year he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Stores and Drafter of Imperial Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the seventh year he was summoned to court; the following year he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Stores and drafter of imperial documents.

sentences.zh: 九年，出知廣州，是歲，加水部郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out to govern Guangzhou; that year he was given the additional title of Director of the Ministry of Water Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he went out as prefect of Guangzhou; that year he was given the additional title of Director in the Ministry of Water Works.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，就遷比部郎中，充樞密直學士，賜金紫，依舊知州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was promoted in place to Director of the Ministry of Punishments, appointed Academician-on-Call of the Bureau of Military Affairs, granted gold seal and purple robe, and continued to govern the prefecture as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was promoted in place to Director in the Ministry of Punishments, appointed Academician-on-Call of the Bureau of Military Affairs, granted gold seal and purple robe, and continued to govern the prefecture as before.

sentences.zh: 休復與轉運使王延範不協，乃奏延範私養術士，厚待過客，撫部下吏有恩，發書與故人韋務昇作隱語，偵朝廷事，反狀已具。

translations.literal: Xiufu did not get along with Transport Commissioner Wang Yanfan; he therefore memorialized that Yanfan privately kept ritual specialists, lavishly entertained traveling guests, showed favor to subordinate officials, sent letters to his old acquaintance Wei Wusheng in covert language, and spied on court affairs—the evidence of rebellion was already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu was at odds with transport commissioner Wang Yanfan; he memorialized that Yanfan secretly kept ritual specialists, lavishly entertained travelers, showed favor to subordinates, sent letters to his old friend Wei Wusheng in hidden language, and spied on court affairs—the case for treason was complete.

sentences.zh: 詔遣內侍閻承翰與休復同按劾之，遂抵於法。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the inner attendant Yan Chenghan to investigate jointly with Xiufu; he was accordingly prosecuted to the full extent of the law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the inner attendant Yan Chenghan to investigate with Xiufu; Yanfan was brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加左諫議大夫，召為戶部使。

translations.literal: Early in Duangong he was given Left Remonstrating Censor and summoned as Revenue Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he was made Left Remonstrating Censor and summoned as Revenue Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，罷使，遷給事中，連知青、潞二州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua the commission was abolished; he was promoted to Supervisor in the Secretariat and in succession governed Qing and Lu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunhua the commission was abolished; he was promoted to Supervisor in the Secretariat and in succession governed Qing and Lu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 休復先上言，以父母槁葬青社，願得領州事，因營丘壟。

translations.literal: Xiufu had earlier submitted a statement that his parents lay in rough burial in the Qing region and he wished to obtain a prefectural post so as to arrange their tomb mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu had earlier memorialized that his parents lay in rough burial in the Qing region and he wished to obtain a prefecture so he could tend their graves.

sentences.zh: 至青州逾年，但聚財殖貨，終不言葬事。

translations.literal: When he reached Qingzhou for more than a year, he only amassed wealth and goods, and to the end never spoke of burial matters.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year at Qingzhou he only amassed wealth and goods and never once spoke of the burial.

sentences.zh: 至潞州數月，瘍生於腦。

translations.literal: After several months at Luzhou, a carbuncle arose in his brain.
translations.idiomatic: After several months at Luzhou a carbuncle formed in his head.

sentences.zh: 既而疾甚，若見王延範，休復但號呼稱死罪，後數日卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: Before long his illness grew severe; it was as if he saw Wang Yanfan—Xiufu only cried out confessing capital guilt, and a few days later died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: His illness soon worsened; he seemed to see Wang Yanfan and could only cry out confessing a capital crime; a few days later he died, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 休復無他能，掌誥命甚不稱職，履行不見稱於搢紳云。

translations.literal: Xiufu had no other ability; in charge of edicts he was very unfit for office, and his conduct was not praised among the gentry, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu had no other talent; as drafter of edicts he was quite unfit, and his conduct won no praise among officials, it is said.

sentences.zh: 張觀，字仲賓，常州毗陵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guan, courtesy name Zhongbin, was a native of Piling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan, whose courtesy name was Zhongbin, came from Piling in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 在江南登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 歸宋，為彭原主簿。

translations.literal: After submitting to Song, he served as Registrar of Pengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to Song he served as registrar of Pengyuan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，移興元府掾，復舉進士不第，調雞澤主簿。

translations.literal: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he was transferred as staff member of Xingyuan Prefecture, took the jinshi examination again without success, and was assigned as Registrar of Jize.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he was transferred as staff member of Xingyuan Prefecture, failed the jinshi examination again, and was assigned registrar of Jize.

sentences.zh: 再求試，特授忠武掌書記，就改觀察判官。

translations.literal: He sought to try the examination again; he was specially appointed Secretary to the Zhongwu Military Commission, and then changed to Administrative Aide of the Inspection Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He sought to try the examination again and was specially appointed secretary to the Zhongwu military commission, then made administrative aide of the inspection commission.

sentences.zh: 上請復刺史及不遣武德卒詣外州偵事，頗稱旨，召拜監察御史，充桂陽監使。

translations.literal: He memorialized the throne requesting restoration of regional prefects and that Wude troops not be sent to outer prefectures to spy on affairs; this greatly accorded with the emperor's wishes; he was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor and Commissioner of Guiyang Supervisorate.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting restoration of regional prefects and that Wude troops not be sent to outer prefectures as spies; this greatly pleased the emperor, and he was summoned as Investigating Censor and commissioner of the Guiyang supervisorate.

sentences.zh: 獻所業文，賜進士及第。

translations.literal: He presented his own literary compositions and was granted jinshi with honors.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his literary compositions and was granted jinshi with honors.

sentences.zh: 會三司言劍外賦稅輕，詔觀乘傳按行諸州，因令稍增之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Three Departments reported that taxes beyond Jianmen were light; an edict ordered Guan to travel post-haste to inspect the various prefectures and thereby to have them slightly increased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Departments reported that taxes beyond Jianmen were light, an edict ordered Guan to travel post-haste through the prefectures and have them slightly increased.

sentences.zh: 觀上疏言：「遠民不宜輕動撓，因而撫之，猶慮其失所，況增賦以擾之乎？

translations.literal: Guan submitted a memorial saying: "The distant people should not be lightly disturbed; even to comfort them one still fears they will lose their footing—how much more to increase levies and harass them?
translations.idiomatic: Guan memorialized, "The distant people should not be lightly disturbed; even pacifying them still risks their losing their livelihood—how much more to raise taxes and harass them?

sentences.zh: 設使積粟流衍，用輸京師，愈煩漕輓，固不可也。

translations.literal: Even supposing grain were piled in surplus and overflowed, to transport it to the capital would only add to the trouble of grain transport—this certainly cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Even if grain piled up in surplus and were sent to the capital, it would only add to the burden of transport—that surely cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 或以分兵就食，亦非安存之策，徒斂怨於民，未見國家之利。」

translations.literal: Or if troops were dispersed to live off local grain, that too is not a policy for secure preservation; it would only gather resentment from the people and bring no benefit to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Nor is dispersing troops to live off local grain a policy for secure rule; it would only breed popular resentment without benefit to the state."

sentences.zh: 太宗深以為然，因留不遣。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply agreed and therefore kept him from being sent.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong strongly agreed and kept him from being sent.

sentences.zh: 其後，復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereafter he again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he again submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 「臣憑借光寵，備位風憲，每遇百官起居日，分立於庭，司察不如儀者舉之。

translations.literal: " Your servant, relying on imperial favor, holds a post in the censorial office; whenever the hundred officials attend levee days, I stand apart in the courtyard and am charged to report anyone whose demeanor is not proper.
translations.idiomatic: " Relying on imperial favor, your servant holds a post in the censorate; on days when the hundred officials attend levee, I stand apart in the courtyard and am charged to report anyone whose bearing is improper.

sentences.zh: 因見陛下天慈優容，多與近臣論政，德音往復，頗亦煩勞。

translations.literal: For I have observed Your Majesty's heavenly kindness and lenience—you often discuss government with close ministers, imperial words going back and forth, which is also rather taxing.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed Your Majesty's heavenly kindness and forbearance: you often discuss government with close ministers, imperial words going back and forth—a considerable burden.

sentences.zh: 至於有司職官，承意將順，簿書叢脞，咸以上聞，豈徒褻黷至尊，實亦輕紊國體。

translations.literal: As for the functional officials of the departments, echoing intentions and catering in compliance, cluttering documents great and small—all report upward. This not only profanes the Supreme One; it truly also lightly disorders the body politic.
translations.idiomatic: Department officials echo your intent and cater in compliance; documents great and small all go up. This not only profanes the sovereign; it truly disorders the body politic.

sentences.zh: 況帝王之道，言則左史書之，動則右史書之，列於緗素，垂為軌範，不可不慎也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Way of emperor and king—when there is speech the left scribe records it; when there is action the right scribe records it; set down in silk and plain, handed down as standards—not to be undertaken carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the way of emperors and kings speech is recorded by the left scribe and action by the right; set down on silk and handed down as models—this cannot be done carelessly.

sentences.zh: 若夫方今之急者，遠人未服，邊鄙不寧。

translations.literal: As for what is urgent today: distant peoples are not yet submissive, and the borderlands are not yet tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: As for today's urgent matters: distant peoples are not yet submissive and the frontiers are not yet secure.

sentences.zh: 陰陽未序，倉廩猶虛。

translations.literal: Yin and yang are not yet in order, and the granaries are still empty.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang are not yet in order and the granaries are still empty.

sentences.zh: 淳樸未還，奢風尚熾。

translations.literal: Simplicity has not yet returned, and extravagant customs still blaze.
translations.idiomatic: Plain living has not yet returned and extravagant ways still burn bright.

sentences.zh: 縣道未治，逋逃尚多。

translations.literal: The districts and circuits are not yet well governed, and fugitives are still numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Districts and circuits are not yet well governed and fugitives are still many.

sentences.zh: 刑法未措，禁令猶密。

translations.literal: Penal law is not yet set aside, and prohibitions are still strict.
translations.idiomatic: Penal law is not yet laid aside and prohibitions remain strict.

sentences.zh: 墜典未復，封祀猶闕。

translations.literal: Fallen rites are not yet restored, and the feng and shan sacrifices are still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Fallen rites are not yet restored and the feng and shan sacrifices are still unperformed.

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，皆朝廷之急務也。

translations.literal: All these several matters are urgent affairs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: All these are urgent affairs of the court.

sentences.zh: 誠願陛下聽斷之暇，宴息之餘，體貌大臣，以之揚榷，使沃心造膝，極意論思，則治體化源，何所不至？

translations.literal: I earnestly wish that in the leisure after Your Majesty's hearing and deciding, in the rest after banquets, you would honor great ministers, use them for weighing and measuring, let them pour out their hearts knee to knee and discourse to the utmost—then the foundations of governance and the wellsprings of transformation, where would they not reach?
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly wish that in the leisure after hearings and in rest after banquets Your Majesty would honor great ministers, weigh matters with them, let them speak heart to heart and discourse to the utmost—then the foundations of rule and the springs of transformation, where would they not reach?

sentences.zh: 臣又嘗讀唐史，見貞觀初始置崇文館，命學士、耆儒更直互進，聽朝之際，則入內殿講論文義，商榷時政。

translations.literal: Your servant has also read the Tang History and seen that at the beginning of Zhenguan they first established the Hall for Venerating Literature, appointing academicians and elder Confucians to rotate duty in turn; at the time of audience they entered the inner hall to expound literary meaning and discuss timely government.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also read the Tang History and seen that at the beginning of Zhenguan they first established the Hall for Venerating Literature, appointing academicians and elder scholars to rotate in attendance; at audience they entered the inner hall to expound the classics and discuss current affairs.

sentences.zh: 或日旰忘倦，或宵分始罷，書諸信史，垂為不朽。

translations.literal: Sometimes forgetting weariness at sundown, sometimes only stopping at midnight division—recorded in the faithful histories, handed down as imperishable.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes forgetting weariness until sundown, sometimes not finishing until midnight—written in the faithful histories and handed down imperishably.

sentences.zh: 況陛下左右前後，皆端士偉人，伏望釋循常之務，養浩然之氣，深詔近臣，闡揚玄風，上為祖宗播無疆之休，下為子孫建不拔之業。

translations.literal: Moreover, to Your Majesty's left and right, before and behind, all are upright scholars and great men; I look up hoping you will set aside routine tasks, nurture the vast qi, deeply instruct close ministers, and unfold the profound Way—above to spread boundless blessing for the ancestors, below to establish an unshakable enterprise for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those at Your Majesty's left and right, before and behind, are all upright scholars and great men; I hope you will set aside routine business, nurture the vast spirit, deeply instruct close ministers, and unfold the profound Way—above to spread boundless blessing for the ancestors, below to build an unshakable foundation for posterity.

sentences.zh: 與夫較量金穀，剖析毫厘，以有限之光陰，役無涯之細務者，安可同年而語哉！」

translations.literal: Compared with weighing gold and grain, parsing every hair's breadth, using limited light and shadow to toil at boundless trifles—how can these be spoken of in the same year!"
translations.idiomatic: Compared with weighing gold and grain, parsing every hair's breadth, spending limited days on endless trifles—how can these be mentioned in the same breath!"

sentences.zh: 上覽而稱之，召賜緋魚，以為度支判官。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and praised it, summoned him and granted crimson robe and fish tally, and made him Aide in the Revenue Accounts Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and praised it, summoned him, granted crimson robe and fish tally, and made him aide in the Revenue Accounts Bureau.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷左司，改鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to the Left Department and changed to Salt and Iron Aide.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to the Left Department and made Salt and Iron aide.

sentences.zh: 嘗因奏事白上曰：「陛下務敦淳化，殿宇采飾，皆徹去之，惟尚樸素，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: On one occasion, while memorializing on affairs, he told the emperor: "Your Majesty is devoted to promoting pure transformation; palace halls and decorative ornament have all been removed—only plain simplicity is honored; the realm is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while memorializing on affairs, he told the emperor, "Your Majesty is devoted to promoting pure transformation; palace ornament has all been stripped away in favor of plain simplicity—the realm is greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 然於服御器用，臣願亦從純儉。」

translations.literal: Yet as for robes and vessels in daily use, your servant wishes that these too follow pure frugality."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in robes and daily vessels, your servant wishes that Your Majesty follow pure frugality as well."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕庶事簡約，至於所服，多用絁絹，皆經浣濯爾，卿言甚善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In all affairs your servant keeps things simple; as for what is worn, much uses coarse silk, all having been washed—your words are very good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In all matters I keep things simple. As for what I wear, I use mostly coarse silk that has all been washed. Your words are excellent."

sentences.zh: 觀頓首謝。

translations.literal: Guan bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Guan bowed his head in thanks.

sentences.zh: 觀數在省署及長春殿次中，諮事於其使李惟清，辨說牴牾，失禮容，惟清不能甘，因奏解其任。

translations.literal: Guan several times in the provincial offices and at his post in the Hall of Everlasting Spring consulted the commissioner Li Weiqing on affairs; their arguments clashed and he lost proper demeanor; Weiqing could not bear it and therefore memorialized to have him removed from his post.
translations.idiomatic: Several times in the provincial offices and at his post in the Hall of Everlasting Spring Guan consulted commissioner Li Weiqing; their arguments clashed and he lost proper demeanor; Weiqing could not endure it and memorialized to have him removed.

sentences.zh: 觀抗章論列，上亦察其無失，故未幾復授舊職。

translations.literal: Guan submitted a memorial in rebuttal setting forth his case; the emperor also saw that he had not erred, and therefore before long restored him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Guan submitted a memorial arguing his case; the emperor also saw he had done no wrong, and before long restored him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 又諫罷治佛寺，不報。

translations.literal: He also remonstrated requesting an end to building Buddhist temples; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He also remonstrated to stop building Buddhist temples; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 俄出為諸路茶鹽制置副使，上疏言更茶鹽之制，於理非便，不合旨，改知黃州，遷揚州，皆有善政。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Deputy Commissioner for Tea and Salt on the various circuits; he memorialized that changing the tea and salt system was in principle inconvenient, did not accord with the intent, was changed to govern Huangzhou, transferred to Yangzhou, and in both places had good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as deputy commissioner for tea and salt on the circuits; he memorialized that changing the tea and salt system was in principle unwise, did not accord with intent, was made prefect of Huangzhou, transferred to Yangzhou, and in both had good administration.

sentences.zh: 會三司改舊貫，均州縣之籍以分其職，召為三司河東道判官。

translations.literal: It happened that the Three Departments changed old practice, equalizing prefectural and county registers to divide their duties; he was summoned as Aide on the Hedong Circuit of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Departments changed old practice and equalized prefectural and county registers to divide duties, he was summoned as aide on the Hedong circuit of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 有詔計司官屬不得越局言他事，觀自以任諫官，乃上書指陳拾遺補闕之職，言事固當然，不奉詔。

translations.literal: There was an edict that officials of the Revenue Office must not overstep their bureau to speak on other matters; Guan considered himself to hold the post of remonstrating official and therefore submitted a letter pointing out the duty of presenting remonstrance and supplying omissions—speaking on affairs was certainly as it should be—and did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said Revenue Office officials must not overstep their bureau to speak on other matters; Guan considered himself a remonstrating official and submitted a letter stating that the duty of remonstrance and supplying omissions made speaking on affairs proper, and did not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 上怒，謂宰相曰：「朕俾警三司僚屬各率其職，非令諫官不言時務，觀乃妄有援引，以諷刺朕，姑為容忍，不欲深責。」

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and said to the chief counselor: "Your servant instructed and warned the Three Departments' subordinates each to fulfill his duty—not ordering remonstrating officials not to speak on timely affairs. Guan presumptuously made citations to satirize your servant; for now your servant tolerates it and does not wish to punish deeply."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and said to the chief counselor, "I instructed the Three Departments' subordinates each to fulfill his duty—I did not order remonstrating officials not to speak on timely affairs. Guan presumptuously cited precedent to satirize me; for now I tolerate it and do not wish to punish deeply."

sentences.zh: 乃令出知道州，移廣南西路轉運使。

translations.literal: He then ordered him out as prefect of Daozhou and transferred him as transport commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered him out as prefect of Daozhou and transferred him as transport commissioner of the Guangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐奏交州黎桓為亂兵所殺、丁濬復位事不實，被劾。

translations.literal: He was impeached because his memorial that Li Huan of Jiaozhou had been killed by mutinous troops and Ding Jun had been restored was not factual.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached because his memorial that Li Huan of Jiaozhou had been killed by mutinous troops and Ding Jun had been restored was not factual.

sentences.zh: 獄未具，卒於桂州，年五十三。

translations.literal: Before the case was concluded he died at Guizhou, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before the case was concluded he died at Guizhou, at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 觀廣覽《漢》、《史》，雅好論事，辭理切直，有古人之風焉。

translations.literal: Guan read widely in the Book of Han and the Records of the Historian, loved by nature to discuss affairs; his reasoning was sharp and direct, with the manner of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Guan read widely in the Book of Han and the Records of the Historian, loved to discuss affairs by nature, and argued with sharp, direct reasoning in the manner of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 論曰：保勳從其子以死事，宋璫忘其身以恤民，臧丙信友誼以明枉，其所履歷，皆有足觀。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Baoxun followed his son in death for the state; Song Dang forgot himself to comfort the people; Zang Bing trusted friendship to clarify a wrong—all that they traversed in office has points worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Baoxun followed his son in dying for the state; Song Dang forgot himself to comfort the people; Zang Bing trusted friendship to clear a wrongful death—what they accomplished in office all has merit worth noting.

sentences.zh: 中正粗振風紀而峻深寡恕，袁廓剛狷誇誕以徼寵任，承恭平恕知止而好佞佛，固皆未盡於善。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng roughly stirred wind and discipline but was stern, deep, and sparing in forgiveness; Yuan Kuo was stubborn, narrow, boastful, and absurd in seeking favor and trust; Chenggong was even-tempered, forgiving, knew when to stop yet doted on Buddhism—they all fell short of goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng roughly revived discipline but was harsh and unforgiving; Yuan Kuo was stubborn, narrow, boastful, and absurd in seeking favor; Chenggong was even-tempered, knew when to stop, yet doted on Buddhism—all fell short of true goodness.

sentences.zh: 知古首獻征南之謀，遂階試用，而其攬轡舊都，猶尋宿怨，與昔人所謂不以私怨惡廢鄉黨之好者異矣。

translations.literal: Zhigu was first to present the plan to conquer the south and thereby rose to trial appointment; yet when he took the reins in his old capital he still sought old grudges—this differs from what the ancients called not letting private resentment overturn liking for one's home district.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigu was first to offer the plan to conquer the south and thereby rose to office; yet when he governed his old capital he still pursued old grudges—unlike the ancients who said one should not let private resentment overturn regard for one's home district.

sentences.zh: 郭載肆為矯誣，而懷恚以死；

translations.literal: Guo Zai wantonly practiced fraud and deceit, yet harbored resentment until death;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zai practiced fraud and deceit wantonly, yet died nursing resentment;

sentences.zh: 休復虧慎終之孝，而樂致人於禍，庸何議焉？

translations.literal: Xiufu failed in filial care at the end and took pleasure in bringing others to disaster—what is there to discuss?
translations.idiomatic: Xiufu failed in filial duty at the end and took pleasure in bringing others to ruin—what is there to discuss?

sentences.zh: 若觀之獻納忠讜，識達體要，則又可嘉者也。

translations.literal: As for Guan, in presenting loyal remonstrance and penetrating essential principles—he may again be commended.
translations.idiomatic: As for Guan, in presenting loyal remonstrance and grasping essential principles, he may again be commended.

sentences.zh: 陳從信

translations.literal: Chen Congxin
translations.idiomatic: Chen Congxin

sentences.zh: 陳從信，字思齊，亳州永城人。

translations.literal: Chen Congxin, courtesy name Siqi, was a native of Yongcheng in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Congxin, whose courtesy name was Siqi, came from Yongcheng in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 恭謹強力，心計精敏。

translations.literal: He was respectful, cautious, strong, and forceful, with a keen and subtle mind for calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He was respectful, cautious, strong, and forceful, with a keen and subtle mind for figures.

sentences.zh: 太宗在晉邸，令典財用，王宮事無大小悉委焉。

translations.literal: When Taizong was at the Jin princely establishment, he had him manage finances; matters of the princely palace great and small were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was at the Jin princely establishment he had him manage finances; great and small affairs of the princely palace were all entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 累官右知客押衙。

translations.literal: He rose in office to Right Reception Vice-Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in office to Right Reception Vice-Marshal.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年秋，三司言倉儲月給，止及明年二月，請分屯諸軍盡率民船，以資江、淮漕運。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year of Kaibao, the Three Departments reported that monthly disbursements from the granaries would last only until the second month of the coming year; they requested that garrisons in the various armies all press the people for boats to supply Jiang-Huai grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the third year of Kaibao the Three Departments reported that monthly granary disbursements would last only until the second month of the coming year and requested that troops in the various armies press the people for boats to supply Jiang-Huai grain transport.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，責之曰：「國無九年之蓄曰不足，爾不素計而使倉儲垂盡，乃請屯兵括民船以運，是可卒致乎？

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly angered and rebuked him, saying: "When a state lacks nine years' stores it is called insufficient—you made no long-term reckoning and let the granaries nearly run dry, yet now ask to station troops and requisition the people's boats for transport; can that be brought about in a hurry?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu flew into a rage and rebuked him: "A state without nine years' grain in reserve is unprepared—you never planned ahead and let the storehouses run nearly empty, yet now you ask to quarter troops and press the people for boats; can that be done overnight?

sentences.zh: 今設汝安用？

translations.literal: Of what use is it to keep you now?
translations.idiomatic: What good are you to me now?

sentences.zh: 苟有所闕，當罪汝以謝眾！」

translations.literal: If anything falls short, you shall be punished to answer to the multitude!"
translations.idiomatic: If anything goes wrong, you will answer for it before the people!"

sentences.zh: 三司使楚昭輔懼，詣太宗求寬釋，使得盡力。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Three Departments Chu Zhaofu was afraid; he went to Taizong to beg leniency so that he might be allowed to exert himself fully.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Three Departments Chu Zhaofu was terrified; he went to Taizong to beg release from blame so he could throw himself into the work.

sentences.zh: 太宗既許，召從信問之，對曰：「從信嘗遊楚、泗，知糧運之患。

translations.literal: Once Taizong had agreed, he summoned Congxin and questioned him; he replied: "Congxin once traveled through Chu and Si and knows the troubles of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong agreed, he summoned Congxin and asked his view. Congxin answered: "I once traveled through Chu and Si and know the troubles of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 良以舟人之食，日歷郡縣勘給，是以凝滯。

translations.literal: It is precisely because boatmen's rations are issued day by day as they pass through commanderies and counties for verification and supply that transport is bogged down.
translations.idiomatic: Boatmen's provisions are doled out day by day as they pass each commandery and county for audit and issue—that is why transport stalls.

sentences.zh: 若自發舟計日往復並支，可以責其程限。

translations.literal: If when the boat departs one calculates the round trip by days and pays out in a lump sum, one can hold them to a schedule.
translations.idiomatic: If each boat is paid for the full round trip by the day when it sets out, their progress can be held to a fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 又楚、泗運米於舟，至京復輦入倉，宜宿備運卒，令即時出納，如此，每運可減數十日。

translations.literal: Moreover, Chu and Si ship grain by boat; when it reaches the capital it is carted again into the granaries—transport soldiers should be kept on standby so that loading and unloading are immediate; in this way each shipment can be shortened by several tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from Chu and Si goes by boat, then at the capital is carted into the granaries again. Keep transport troops on standby for instant loading and unloading—each run could be cut by many days.

sentences.zh: 楚、泗至京千里，舊八十日一運，一歲三運。

translations.literal: From Chu and Si to the capital is a thousand li; formerly one shipment took eighty days, three shipments a year.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Si lie a thousand li from the capital; formerly one run took eighty days, three runs a year.

sentences.zh: 若去淹留之虛日，則歲可增一運焉。

translations.literal: If the empty days lost to delay are removed, the year can gain one more shipment.
translations.idiomatic: Strip out the wasted days of delay and the year could gain an extra run.

sentences.zh: 今三司欲籍民舟，若不許，則無以責辦，許之，則冬中京師薪炭殆絕矣。

translations.literal: Now the Three Departments wish to register civilian boats; if this is not permitted, there is no way to hold anyone responsible for fulfillment, but if permitted, in midwinter fuel and charcoal in the capital will nearly run out.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments want to register civilian boats—refuse and nothing gets done; agree and midwinter fuel and charcoal in the capital will nearly vanish.

sentences.zh: 不若募舟之堅者漕糧，其損敗者任載薪炭，則公私俱濟。

translations.literal: Better to recruit the sturdiest boats for grain transport by canal and assign the damaged ones to carry fuel and charcoal; then public and private interests will both be served.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hire the sturdiest boats for grain transport and let damaged ones carry fuel and charcoal—both public and private needs would be met.

sentences.zh: 今市米騰貴，官價斗錢七十，賈者失利，無敢致於京師，雖居商厚儲亦匿而不糶，是以米益貴，民將餓殍。

translations.literal: Now market rice has soared in price; the official price is seventy cash per dou; merchants lose money and none dare bring grain to the capital; even wealthy dealers hoard heavily and will not sell, so rice grows dearer still and the people will starve to death in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Market rice has soared; the official price is seventy cash per dou, so merchants lose money and none dare ship to the capital. Even wealthy dealers hoard and refuse to sell—rice grows dearer and the people face starvation.

sentences.zh: 若聽民自便，即四方奔湊，米多而價自賤矣。」

translations.literal: If the people are allowed to act as they please, grain will rush in from the four quarters; with much rice the price will naturally fall."
translations.idiomatic: Let the people trade freely and grain will pour in from every direction—abundance will bring the price down of itself."

sentences.zh: 太宗明日具奏，太祖可之，其事果集焉。

translations.literal: The next day Taizong presented the full report; Taizu approved it, and the matter was indeed carried through.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Taizong laid the plan before the throne; Taizu approved, and the scheme succeeded.

sentences.zh: 從信好方術，有李八百者，自言八百歲，從信事之甚謹，冀傳其術，竟無所得。

translations.literal: Congxin was fond of esoteric arts; there was one Li Babai who claimed to be eight hundred years old; Congxin served him with great reverence, hoping to receive his techniques, but in the end obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Congxin dabbled in esoteric arts. A man called Li Babai claimed to be eight hundred years old; Congxin served him devoutly in hope of learning his secrets but gained nothing in the end.

sentences.zh: 又侯莫陳利用者，所為多不法，始因從信推薦，人以是少之。

translations.literal: There was also Houmochen Liyong, whose conduct was largely unlawful; he had first come in through Congxin's recommendation, and for this people thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Houmochen Liyong, whom Congxin had recommended, behaved largely outside the law—and for that people thought less of Congxin.

sentences.zh: 張平，青州臨朐人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ping was a native of Linqu in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping came from Linqu in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠寓單州，依刺史羅金山。

translations.literal: In his weak-crown years he lodged in Dan Prefecture and attached himself to the prefect Luo Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he lived in Dan Prefecture under the patronage of Prefect Luo Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 金山移滁州，署平馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: When Jinshan was transferred to Chu Prefecture, he appointed Ping Chief Commandant of Horse and Foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinshan moved to Chu Prefecture, he appointed Ping Chief Commandant of Horse and Foot.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京兆，置其邸。

translations.literal: When Taizong served as prefectural governor of Jingzhao, he placed Ping in his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong governed Jingzhao, he took Ping into his household.

sentences.zh: 及秦王廷美領貴州，復署為親吏。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin Tingmei held Guizhou, he again appointed him a personal attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qin Tingmei held Guizhou, Ping was again made a personal attendant.

sentences.zh: 後數年，有譖平匿府中錢物，秦王白太宗鞫之，無狀，秦王益不喜，遂遣去。

translations.literal: Several years later someone slandered Ping for concealing money and goods in the princely mansion; the Prince of Qin reported this to Taizong for investigation; no evidence was found, but the prince liked him even less and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Years later someone accused Ping of hiding valuables in the princely mansion. Prince of Qin told Taizong to investigate; nothing was proved, but the prince liked him less and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 太宗憐其非罪，以屬徐帥高繼冲，繼冲署為鎮將。

translations.literal: Taizong pitied him as innocent of wrongdoing and handed him over to the military governor of Xu, Gao Jichong, who appointed him garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, pitying his innocence, gave him to Xu military governor Gao Jichong, who made him garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 平歎曰：「吾命雖蹇，後未必不為福也。」

translations.literal: Ping sighed and said: "Though my fate is hard, later it may yet turn to blessing."
translations.idiomatic: Ping sighed: "My lot is bitter, but later it may yet prove a blessing."

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，召還，同知三班事，遷如京使。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongxi era he was recalled and made Associate Director of the Third Class Bureau; he was promoted to Commissioner on Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongxi he was recalled, made Associate Director of the Third Class Bureau, then promoted Commissioner on Imperial Audience.

sentences.zh: 三年，改西上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate.

sentences.zh: 才三月，又改客省使。

translations.literal: After only three months he was again changed to Commissioner of the Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Three months later he was made Commissioner of the Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 四年，代王明為鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he replaced Wang Ming as Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he replaced Wang Ming as Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 平掌陽平署積年，是秋，聞陝西轉運使李安發其舊為陽平姦利，憂恚成疾而卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: Ping had managed the Yangping Office for many years; that autumn, on hearing that Shaanxi transport commissioner Li An had exposed his old malfeasance and illicit profit at Yangping, he died of grief and indignation at sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Ping had run the Yangping Office for years. That autumn, when he learned Shaanxi transport commissioner Li An had exposed his old graft there, he died of grief and rage at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈右千牛衛上將軍，官給葬具。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended; he was posthumously made General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and funeral goods were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspended audiences. He was posthumously made General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, with state-supplied funeral goods.

sentences.zh: 平好史傳，微時遇異書，盡日耽玩，或解衣易之。

translations.literal: Ping loved historical writings; in humble days when he encountered a rare book he would devote the whole day to it in delight, sometimes stripping off his coat to exchange for it.
translations.idiomatic: Ping loved history. In humble days he would spend whole days poring over any rare book he found, sometimes trading his coat for it.

sentences.zh: 及貴，聚書數千卷。

translations.literal: When he had risen in rank he collected several thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated he amassed several thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 在彭門日，郡吏有侮平者數輩，後悉被罪配京窯務。

translations.literal: While at Peng Gate, several clerks of the prefecture who had insulted Ping were later all convicted and assigned to the capital kiln service.
translations.idiomatic: At Peng Gate several prefectural clerks who had slighted Ping were later convicted and sent to the capital kiln penal service.

sentences.zh: 平子從式適董其役，見之，以語平。

translations.literal: Ping's son Congshi happened to oversee their labor; seeing them, he told Ping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congshi happened to supervise their labor, saw them, and told Ping.

sentences.zh: 平召至第，為設酒饌勞之，曰：「公等不幸，偶罹斯患，慎勿以前為念。」

translations.literal: Ping summoned them to his residence, set out wine and food to comfort them, and said: "You gentlemen have met misfortune and chanced upon this affliction; take care not to dwell on what went before."
translations.idiomatic: Ping summoned them home, feasted them, and said: "You have met ill fortune in this punishment; do not brood on the past."

sentences.zh: 給以緡錢，且戒從式善視之。

translations.literal: He gave them cash and also charged Congshi to treat them well.
translations.idiomatic: He gave them cash and told Congshi to look after them kindly.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遇赦得原，時人稱其寬厚。

translations.literal: Before long they met an amnesty and were pardoned; people of the time praised his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an amnesty freed them; contemporaries praised his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 從式事太宗藩邸，累官文思使。

translations.literal: Congshi served at Taizong's princely establishment and rose in office to Commissioner of Literary Ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi had served Taizong's princely household and rose to Commissioner of Literary Ingenuity.

sentences.zh: 子 從吉

translations.literal: Son Congji
translations.idiomatic: Son Congji

sentences.zh: 次子從吉，以蔭補殿直，轉供奉官、知宜州，屢破溪蠻。

translations.literal: The second son Congji entered office by yin privilege as a palace attendant, became an imperial attendant, and served as prefect of Yi Prefecture, repeatedly defeating the stream barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, Congji, entered service by yin privilege as palace attendant, became imperial attendant, and governed Yi Prefecture, repeatedly defeating the stream tribes.

sentences.zh: 轉運使堯叟上其狀，累遷內殿崇班、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Yaoshou submitted a report on his achievements; he was repeatedly promoted to Inner Hall Honored Ban and Palace Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Yaoshou reported his achievements; he rose repeatedly to Inner Hall Honored Ban and Palace Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 在任凡八年，代還，為如京副使。

translations.literal: In office eight years in all, when replaced he became Deputy Commissioner on Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in office he returned and was made Deputy Commissioner on Imperial Audience.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，知環州，嘗與宋沆率兵襲西夏，小衄，部署張凝表其專，責授內殿崇班。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he governed Huan Prefecture; he once joined Song Hang in leading troops to raid Western Xia, suffered a minor setback, and deployment commissioner Zhang Ning memorialized his arbitrariness; he was demoted to Inner Hall Honored Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianping he governed Huan Prefecture, joined Song Hang in a raid on Western Xia, met a minor reverse, and deployment commissioner Zhang Ning accused him of overstepping; he was demoted to Inner Hall Honored Ban.

sentences.zh: 俄知澧州，復舊秩。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Li Prefecture and restored to his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he governed Li Prefecture and regained his former rank.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，宜州軍校陳進叛，命副曹利用為廣南東、西路安撫使，將兵討之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, when the Yi Prefecture garrison officer Chen Jin rebelled, he was appointed deputy to Cao Liyong as Pacification Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Routes of Guangnan and led troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4, when Yi Prefecture officer Chen Jin rebelled, he was named deputy to Cao Liyong as Pacification Commissioner of Eastern and Western Guangnan and marched against him.

sentences.zh: 次象州大鳥砦，與賊戰，進為先鋒郭志言所刺，遂入城，斬首六十級。

translations.literal: Halting at the Great Bird Stockade in Xiang Prefecture, he fought the rebels; Jin was stabbed by the vanguard Guo Zhiyan, then they entered the city and took sixty heads.
translations.idiomatic: At Great Bird Stockade in Xiang Prefecture he fought the rebels; Jin was stabbed by vanguard Guo Zhiyan. They entered the city and took sixty heads.

sentences.zh: 以平賊功，改莊宅副使。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying the rebels he was made Deputy Manager of the Estates.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying the rebels he was made Deputy Manager of the Estates.

sentences.zh: 未還，卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: Before he returned he died at forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died before returning, at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 王繼升

translations.literal: Wang Jisheng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jisheng

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，以諸道水陸發運併為一司，命繼升與刑部員外郎董儼同掌其事，號為稱職。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi the water and land transport offices of the various circuits were merged into one bureau; Jisheng and Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Dong Yan were together ordered to manage it, and they were called competent at their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 the circuit water-and-land transport offices were merged into one bureau; Jisheng and Ministry of Punishments Vice Director Dong Yan were put in charge together and were reckoned competent.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右神武軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to General of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made General of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，改領本州團練使，三月，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: Early in the Duangong era he was changed to command the militia of his home prefecture; in the third month he died at sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he took command of his home prefecture's militia; in the third month he died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 太宗頗嗟悼，贈洋州觀察使，葬事官給。

translations.literal: Taizong sighed in mourning and posthumously made him Military Governor of Yang Prefecture; funeral arrangements were supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him deeply, posthumously made him Military Governor of Yang Prefecture, and supplied the funeral from state funds.

sentences.zh: 子昭遠。

translations.literal: His son was Zhaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 子 昭遠

translations.literal: Son Zhaoyuan
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhaoyuan

sentences.zh: 昭遠，形質魁偉，色黑，繼升名之「鐵山」。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan was of imposing build and dark complexion; Jisheng named him "Iron Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan was tall and dark; Jisheng called him "Iron Mountain."

sentences.zh: 有膂力，善騎射。

translations.literal: He had great physical strength and was skilled at horseback archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was powerfully built and skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 少時入山捕鷹鶻，值澗水暴漲十餘丈，昭遠升大樹，經宿得免。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the mountains to hunt hawks and falcons; he came upon a mountain torrent that rose more than ten zhang in a sudden flood; Zhaoyuan climbed a great tree and after a night was spared.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he hunted hawks in the hills; a flash flood rose more than ten zhang. Zhaoyuan climbed a great tree and survived the night.

sentences.zh: 嘗涉河，冰陷，二人傍共援出之，昭遠神色自若。

translations.literal: Once he crossed a river; the ice gave way and two men at his side together pulled him out; Zhaoyuan's expression was as calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: Once crossing a river he broke through the ice; two companions hauled him out, but his face never changed.

sentences.zh: 喜與里中惡少遊處，一日，眾祀里神，昭遠適至，有以博投授之，謂曰：「汝他日儻有節鉞，試擲以卜之。」

translations.literal: He liked to associate with the village rowdies; one day when the crowd was sacrificing to the village god, Zhaoyuan happened to arrive; someone handed him casting sticks for divination and said: "If someday you perchance hold a commander's seal and staff, try casting to divine it."
translations.idiomatic: He consorted with local rowdies. Once, during a village-god sacrifice, someone handed him divining dice and said: "If you ever win a commander's seal and baton, cast to see."

sentences.zh: 昭遠一擲，六齒皆赤。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan cast once; all six teeth came up red.
translations.idiomatic: He cast once—all six faces came up red.

sentences.zh: 涪王之遷房陵也，禁衛諸校楊均、王榮等以依附被譴，獨昭遠無所預，太宗以為忠。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was moved to Fangling, various commandants of the palace guards Yang Jun and Wang Rong and others were punished for having attached themselves to him; Zhaoyuan alone was not implicated, and Taizong took this as loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Fu was banished to Fangling, guard officers Yang Jun and Wang Rong were punished for clinging to him; Zhaoyuan alone was untouched, and Taizong called it loyalty.

sentences.zh: 再遷東西班都虞候，轉殿前班都指揮使，領寰州刺史。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Chief Commandant of the Eastern and Western Bureaus, then to Chief Commander of the Palace Front Bureau, and held the post of prefect of Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose twice to Chief Commandant of the Eastern and Western Bureaus, then Chief Commander of the Palace Front Bureau, and governed Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改馬步軍都軍頭，命乘傳鎮、定、高陽關，募兵以備契丹。

translations.literal: He was changed to Chief of the Horse and Foot Armies, ordered to travel by express post to Zhen, Ding, and the Gaoyang Pass to recruit troops against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chief of the Horse and Foot Armies, rode express to Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, and recruited troops against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 又為冀州駐泊都監，俄授澤州團練使、洺州都部署。

translations.literal: He also served as garrison commander at Ji Prefecture, and soon received the posts of militia commander of Ze Prefecture and deployment commissioner of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also garrison commander at Ji Prefecture, then militia commander of Ze and deployment commissioner of Ming.

sentences.zh: 太宗屢稱其能，可備急使。

translations.literal: Taizong repeatedly praised his ability and said he could be relied on for urgent missions.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong often praised his ability and said he was fit for urgent duty.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，召為殿前都虞候，領勤州防禦使。

translations.literal: Early in Duangong he was summoned as Chief Commandant of the Palace Front and held the post of Defender of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he was made Chief Commandant of the Palace Front and Defender of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 命有司治綾錦院為公署，掘地得鐵若山形，或言此地即鐵山故營，又與昭遠幼名合，聞者異之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to prepare the Brocade and Damask Bureau as his official residence; when the ground was dug they found iron shaped like a mountain; some said this place was the old camp of Iron Mountain, and it also matched Zhaoyuan's childhood name—hearers found it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to fit out the Brocade Bureau as his headquarters, diggers found iron shaped like a mountain. Some said this was old Iron Mountain camp—and it matched Zhaoyuan's boyhood name. All who heard it marveled.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗草書紈扇，作古詩賜諸將，意多比諷，其賜昭遠，尤加賞遇。

translations.literal: Taizong once wrote ancient verse in cursive on silk fans and bestowed them on the generals; the meaning was largely allegorical and satirical; what he gave Zhaoyuan was especially marked by favor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once wrote ancient verse in cursive on silk fans for his generals—mostly allegorical barbs. Zhaoyuan's fan won especial favor.

sentences.zh: 二年，領沙州觀察使，再為幷、代副都部署。
